news.abstract: Some Iranians are suspicious at sight of US flag being used in official capacity to mark tents housing American relief team after earthquake in Bam; team expects to stay one week, and will work with Iranian Red Crescent to help assess damage to city's infrastructure and draw up list of needs to be distributed to international donors (M)
news.title: An Odd Sight in Iran as Aid Team Tents Go Up: The U.S. Flag

news.abstract: American aid to Iran, granted after the devastating earthquake in the city of Bam, could bring an improvement to the two countries long-frigid relationship.
news.title: Iranians Appear to Warm to Easing Tensions With U.S.

news.abstract: Ukrainian Supreme Court rules that Pres Leonid Kuchma is exempt from Constitution's two-term limit because Constitution itself has only been in place for eight years; opposition party condemns ruling (M)
news.title: New Math Adds Up to an Extended Run for Ukraine's President

news.abstract: Prison warden says Russian oil billionaire Mikhail B Khodorkovsky will be allowed to usher in New Year by watching television, but will not be permitted to sing or drink champagne (M)
news.title: No 'Auld Lang Syne' for Jailed Russian Oilman

news.abstract: United Kingdom, including England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Island, is officially valued at $8.8 trillion; statisticians arrived at figure using new models and more detailed information measuring all private and public assets; some Britons are appalled at expenditure to arrive at valuation; photos (M)
news.title: London Journal; The Sceptered Isle Is Appraised: $8 Trillion and Change

news.abstract: Egyptian government envoy Osama el-Baz meets with embattled Palestinian leader Yasir Arafat in Ramallah; carries letter to Arafat from Pres Hosni Mubarak, who is trying to arrange new meeting of Palestinian faction leaders in hopes of getting them to agree to stop attacks against Israelis; Egyptian-sponsored meeting of dozen Palestinian leaders in Cairo early last month ended in stalemate; Arafat, standing at Baz's side, says little to reporters that would indicate any new initiative is under way; photo (M)
news.title: Egyptian Urges Arafat to Subdue Factions

news.abstract: United States Army in Iraq is increasingly relying on its snipers to protect infantry patrols sweeping through urban streets and alleyways and to kill guerrilla leaders and disrupt their attacks; commanders say snipers are different breed of warrior--quiet, unflappable marksmen who bring dispassionate intensity to their deadly task; demand for snipers is great enough that Army has sent team of trainers to Iraq to keep churning out new ones for war effort there and in other hot spots; sniper school is placing increasing emphasis on urban tactics as Army faces more conflicts like those in Iraq in which terrorists use tight confines of city blocks and rooftops to stage hit-and-run strikes; photo (M)
news.title: In Iraq's Murky Battle, Snipers Offer U.S. a Precision Weapon

news.abstract: Defense Dept confirms death of 480th service member in Iraq since start of Iraq war (S)
news.title: Killed in Iraq

news.abstract: Pres Bush says he welcomes signs of warmer dealings with Iran in recent weeks, but that country must still rid itself of terrorists and nuclear weapons programs and open its political system before he will be ready to improve relations with Iran; direct talks with Iran were suspended in May after series of bombings in Saudi Arabia were traced by American intelligence officials to groups operating in Iran; warm welcome received by American relief workers arriving in earthquake-stricken city of Bam had raised possibility of end to freeze that has lasted since Iranian hostage crisis nearly quarter century ago (M)
news.title: Bush Says Iran Must Do More Before Relations Can Improve

news.abstract: British Airways canceled a mid-afternoon flight from London to Washington today for the second day in a row.
news.title: British Flight Called Off After Security Concerns

news.abstract: Cambodia moves closer to convening trial for deaths of 1.7 million people under brutal rule of Khmer Rouge in 1970's; Khieu Samphan, one of top Khmer Rouge leaders, has begun to plead his case publicly, claiming ignorance, innocence, shock and contrition (M)
news.title: A Top Khmer Rouge Leader, Going Public, Pleads Ignorance

news.abstract: Private delegation of US experts on North Korea, including former National Security Council staff member Jack Pritchard and former Los Alamos National Laboratory dir Sigfried Hecker, will travel to North Korea and possibly visit nuclear weapons plant; Bush administration officials say delegation does not have official government blessing; express concern that trip might complicate administration's own delicate diplomacy with North Korea; John W Lewis, professor emeritus of international relati ons at Stanford University, will lead delegation (M)
news.title: Private Group Prepares Visit To North Korea

news.abstract: Norwegian police arrest Mullah Krekar, spiritual leader of Islamic militant group Ansar al-Islam, on charges of attempted murder in connection with two suicide bombings in northern Iraq in 2002 (M)
news.title: Kurdish Islamic Leader Arrested in Norway on Murder Charges

news.abstract: Brazil is giving poor families small cash payments if they keep their children in school and take them for regular medical checkups; Pres Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva is consolidating array of cash transfer programs, expanding his version of model, named Family Grant, and tripling average monthly benefit, to about $24; Family Grant will reach 11.4 million families by 2006--over 45 million people, about quarter of Brazil's population; that would be world's largest such program; W orld Bank and Inter-American Development Bank are putting up $3 billion in loans for program; Nicaragua, Honduras and Mexico have adopted similar programs; photos (M)
news.title: To Help Poor Be Pupils, Not Wage Earners, Brazil Pays Parents

news.abstract: Bush administration says Iran has rebuffed offer from US to send delegation led by Sen Elizabeth Dole to assist in distribution of relief supplies to earthquake victims in Bam; says Iran cited difficulties facing relief workers in ancient city, but did not rule out possibility of future visit; expresses concern for Iran at time when US has declared that some of Tehran's recent actions have been positive and could lead to resumption of dialogue to improve relations; photo of Muslims praying in damaged mosque (M)
news.title: IRAN TURNS DOWN AMERICAN OFFER OF RELIEF MISSION

news.abstract: Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee of India stepped onto Pakistani soil for the first time in four years, his mere presence feeding the hopes for peace between India and Pakistan.
news.title: India and Pakistan Offer Hint of Thaw

news.abstract: Flash Airlines Boeing 737 en route to Paris crashes shortly after take-off from Sharm el-Sheik, Egypt, killing all 148 people on board, mostly French, Japanese and Moroccan tourists, plus Egyptian crew; crash is tentatively blamed on technical failure, rather than terrorism, though flight recorder has not been recovered; this is third crash of Egyptian commercial airliner in four years; photo, maps (M)
news.title: Egyptian Charter Jet Crashes in Red Sea, Killing 148

news.abstract: Indian Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee visits Pakistan for meeting of South Asian Assn for Regional Cooperation; discussions do not include fate of Kashmir, over which India and Pakistan have repeatedly fought, but visit is seen as tentative step toward improving relations, which hardliners on neither side welcome; there has been 'pent-up demand for people-to-people contact' since Vajpayee extended 'hand of friendship' to Pakistan seven months ago; photo (M)
news.title: Indian Leader's Trip to Pakistan Raises Hope for Warmer Ties

news.abstract: Parmalat founder Calisto Tanzi, in jail on fraud charges, will surrender his stake in insolvent company and some of his personal assets to company's administrator; Tanzi family holds about 50 percent of company; Tanzi does not say whether his offer includes entire holding (S)
news.title: Parmalat Stake to Be Sold

news.abstract: Israeli Army kills four young Palestinians in Nablus, including one during funeral of the others; shootings, including that at funeral procession, were in response to rock throwing and sightings of firebombs or handguns among Palestinian youths and came as Israeli incursion into city enters its second week; photo (M)
news.title: Israelis Kill 4 Palestinians During Operation in Nablus

news.abstract: Bush administration decides to let Kurdish region remain semiautonomous as part of newly sovereign Iraq, despite warnings from Iraq's neighbors and many Iraqis not to divide country into ethnic states; American and Iraqi officials say position on Kurdish area was effectively dictated by Nov 15 accord with Iraqi leaders that established June 30 as target date for Iraqi self-rule; say rapid timetable leaves no time to change autonomy and unity of Kurdish stronghold of north; administration and Iraq officials insist that leaving Kurdish autonomous region intact does not preclude country's consolidating itself without ethnic states in future when Iraq writes its own constitution; say Bush administration will press Iraq not to divide itself permanently along ethic lines; issue of whether Iraq is to be divided into ethnic states in federation-style government is of great significance both inside country and throughout Middle East, where there is widespread fear that dividing Iraq along ethnic or sectarian lines could break country up and spread turmoil throughout region; photo (M)
news.title: Kurdish Region in Northern Iraq Will Get to Keep Special Status

news.abstract: Colombian agents, working with American intelligence operatives, tracked top Colombian guerrilla commander Ricardo Palmera for months before he was arrested on busy street in Quito, Ecuador; Palmera was leading negotiator in peace talks that failed in 2002; Colombian government is calling his capture a major blow against Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia, Marxist rebel group, and proof that Pres Alvaro Uribe's efforts to weaken rebels is working; photo (M)
news.title: Colombians, With U.S. Aid, Tracked Rebel For Months

news.abstract: Communist rebellion in Philippines that began 35 years ago foundered but has regained strength; military estimates there are 10,000 fighters in its armed wing, New People's Army; Philippine military spokesman says Communists are 'utmost security concern' even though they have been overshadowed by Muslim insurgents; says they are much bigger threat than Abu Sayyaf, Moro Islamic Liberation Front or Jemaah Islamiyah (M)
news.title: Fear of a Communist Rebellion Is Growing in the Philippines

news.abstract: New Constitution for Afghanistan is approved by acclamation by 502 delegates at national meeting, concluding three weeks of often tense debate; for first time, Afghans have set up democratic presidential system, with directly elected president and two-chamber national assembly; elections are to be held in just six months; independent judiciary is also being organized; country will be renamed Islamic Republic of Afghanistan, combining democracy and religion; there is to be system of civil law, but no law will be contrary to beliefs and provisions of Islam; new bedrock of government is welcomed by Afghan human rights and women's activists as offering prospect of rule of law in ravaged country; diplomats and foreign experts who observed process praise it for being coherent and even forward looking for region; Pres Bush welcomes new Constitution; Americans hope new arrangements will provide stronger government that can help Afghanistan rebuild after war that defeated Taliban government that had befriended Osama bin Laden; photos; chart with highlights of Afghan pact (L)
news.title: AFGHAN COUNCIL GIVES APPROVAL TO CONSTITUTION

news.abstract: W.H.O. officials today warned that Chinas slaughter, if done improperly, risked the possibility of more infections.
news.title: Risks Seen in Chinas Plan to Slaughter Cats to Fight SARS

news.abstract: United Nations special representative Lakhdar Brahimi, one of main architects of Afghanistan's new Constitution, prepares to bow out after two years in job; Brahimi, an Algerian diplomat, has been loyal ally to Afghans since brokering Bonn accords in Dec 2001 for new Afghan order after defeat of Taliban; is personal friend of Pres Hamid Karzai, and has served in Afghanistan twice; was UN special envoy from 1997 to 1999, during Taliban years; photo (M)
news.title: Kabul Journal; With Future Charted, U.N. Envoy Departs

news.abstract: GEORGIA: Landslide Expected; NEW NATO CHIEF TAKES OVER; FRANCE: Muslims Lash Out At Planned Head Scarf Ban; NORWAY: Islamic Militant Ordered Freed;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: The two countries, which have fought three wars and two years ago nearly fought a fourth, today heralded a new chapter in their relationship.
news.title: India and Pakistan Plan Talks Aiming to Settle Kashmir Dispute

news.abstract: United States Army is preparing order that would require about 7,000 troops now in Iraq, Kuwait and Afghanistan to remain on duty through end of their deployments this spring, even if they could otherwise leave service before then; another order, previously announced, already prevents active-duty and reserve troops rotating into Iraq and Kuwait this year from leaving Army before serving 12 months on ground, plus 90-day period after they return (M)
news.title: Army Delays Discharge for Some G.I.'s in Afghanistan and Mideast

news.abstract: British Foreign Secretary Jack Straw says British troops will stay in Iraq for years, perhaps until 2007, to help restore country's security and stability (S)
news.title: British Aide Sees Long Iraq Stay

news.abstract: Israeli and Libyan officials held a secret meeting in December and discussed the possibility of ties between the longstanding enemies, Israeli officials said today.
news.title: Israeli Officials Report Secret Meeting With Libyans

news.abstract: India and Pakistan agree to restart formal peace talks on all issues, including Kashmir; Pakistan says it will not permit its territory to be used to support terrorism, first such direct assurance to India in more than half century of conflict; agreement follows Prime Min Atal Bihari Vajpayee's meeting with Pakistani Pres Pervez Musharraf and other less publicized negotiations, some during regional summit meeting in Islamabad; photos, one of Vajpayee with Pakistani Prime Min Mir Zafarullah Jamali; map; Musharraf says 'history has been made'; Vajpayee, 79, offers 'hand of friendship' in hopes of leaving legacy of peace; Musharraf's promise to crack down on militants whom Pakistan has long supported, and who are linked to two recent assassination attempts on him, appears to complete U-turn he made after Sept 11, 2001, when he abandoned Pakistan's support for Taliban in Afghanistan; Pakistan in turn wins long-sought dialogue on Kashmir, where it demands right of self-determination by mostly Muslim population (M)
news.title: INDIANS IN DEAL WITH PAKISTANIS FOR PEACE TALKS

news.abstract: Bechtel National wins contract that could be worth $1.82 billion over two years, to help restore power, water and other essential services in Iraq (S)
news.title: Bechtel Wins Its Second Big Contract for Iraq

news.abstract: Canadian soft drink manufacturers will discontinue distribution of soft drinks, including Coca-Cola and Pepsi, for vending machines in Canadian elementary and junior high schools; pressure from politicians, educators and parents to present healthier choices for children precipitated change; high schools will still offer soft drinks (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Canada: Coke And Pepsi To Pull Soda From Schools

news.abstract: Twenty five years after the end of the murderous Khmer Rouge regime, a top Cambodian government official said today that the time had come to put surviving leaders on trial.
news.title: In Cambodia, an Anniversary Renews Call for Genocide Trials

news.abstract: International group of 19 scientists, analyzing research around globe, warns that warming climate will rival habitat destruction in causing widespread species extinctions this century; predict that 15-37 percent of 1,013 species studied will be doomed by 2050 if current warming trends continue; Drs Chris D Thomas and Daniel B Botkin comment on report in journal Nature (M)
news.title: Scientists Predict Widespread Extinction by Global Warming

news.abstract: Greek Prime Min Costas Simitis will call parliamentary election in March, month early, and resign next day, after eight years of leading ruling party (M)
news.title: Greek Prime Minister Says He Will Step Down After Election

news.abstract: Pakistan's decision to end state support for Islamic militants in Kashmir followed eight months of secret talks and assassination attempt that seems to have confirmed Gen Pervez Musharraf's decision; photo (M)
news.title: Sense of Mortality Gave Push to India-Pakistan Talks

news.abstract: Something seems to have come over one of the world's best-known boogeymen, Col. Muammar el-Qaddafi, who after making Libya a pariah in the 1980's, pledged last month to end its illicit arms programs.
news.title: Qaddafi's Surprise: Why a New Stance?

news.abstract: Donald Tsang, Hong Kong's second highest government official, reports that Chinese President Hu Jintao has expressed concern over proposed democratic changes for Hong Kong and has conveyed doubts to Chief Executive Tung Chee-hwa; officials in Beijing have requested further discussion and Hong Kong committee has been appointed to meet with minland government (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Hong Kong: Democracy Side Step

news.abstract: Hundreds of students, who are protesting proposed cuts in university financing, take over building in Leipzig (Germany) where Chancellor Gerhard Schroder is scheduled to sign official application for city to hold 2012 Olympic Games; signing ceremony is moved (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Students Chase Schröder From Building

news.abstract: The attack also wounded dozens and was a further indication of the depth of religious and political animosity in Iraq.
news.title: At Least 4 Killed in Bomb Blast at Mosque in Iraq

news.abstract: GREECE: Foreign Minister Seeks LeaderS Post; GERMANY: Students Chase SchrÖDer From Building; GEORGIA: Region Imposes Emergency; BRITAIN: Tuition Raises Proposed; BRITAIN: Viking Hopes Cruelly Dashed;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Almost no one in United States remembers war that Americans fought against Mexico more than 150 years ago; in Mexico, almost no one has forgotten; war cut Mexico in two and, according to Mexico City historian Miguel Soto, inflicted wound that never really healed; as Pres Bush prepares to fly down to Mexico from Texas, where war began in 1846, debate in Mexico City is over how to relate to US; photo (M)
news.title: Mexico City Journal; Of Gringos and Old Grudges: This Land Is Their Land

news.abstract: Sotheby's in New York will auction nine Imperial Faberge Easter eggs from Czarist Russia that were acquired over lifetime by late publishing magnate Malcolm Forbes; collection is second in size only to 10 in Kremlin; it will be offered in April along with 180 other Faberge objects from Forbes holdings; together they are expected to sell for at least $90 million; growing number of newly rich Russian collectors have added to strength of this market; another potential buyer is Kremlin, which might want to add to its trove of Imperial eggs; extraordinary materials and workmanship that went into eggs, coupled with their size (six inches of less) make them perhaps most luxurious, over-the-top baubles ever produced; Malcolm Forbes' son Christopher says he and his siblings have been receiving offers from collectors all over world willing to pay handsomely for their eggs; photo (M)
news.title: Fabled Trove of Fabergé Eggs Goes to Auction, Jewels and All

news.abstract: Swiss police arrest eight foreign nationals suspected of involvement in suicide bomb attacks in May 2003 in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, that killed 35 people (S)
news.title: Swiss Hold 8 Suspects in Saudi Attacks

news.abstract: Hong Kong Court of Final Appeal blocks government plans to fill in section of Victoria Harbor for proposed covered highway; requires government show overriding public need to carry out plan (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Hong Kong: Harbor Reprieve

news.abstract: Brazil and US are holding fast to their insistence on photographing and fingerprinting visitors from other country; what began as minor spat is threatening to sour relations between two countries; dispute grew out of new US security program that applies to all foreigners entering country who are required to have visas; US has identified border region where Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay come together as haven for Islamic terrorists (M)
news.title: U.S. and Brazil Fingerprinting: Is It Getting Out of Hand?

news.abstract: Defense Dept designates Saddam Hussein as prisoner of war, legal status that sets standards for how he is treated and allows International Committee of Red Cross to see him; information about Hussein has been tightly guarded, although members of Iraqi Governing Council were allowed to confirm his identity; senior US officials say FBI has become increasingly involved in questioning Hussein, signaling that authorities view him as potential defendant in legal proceeding as well as intelligence source; CIA remains in overall control, but FBI involvement reflects CIA reluctance to allow covert officers to take part in interrogations that could force them to appear as court witnesses (M)
news.title: Hussein Given P.O.W. Status; Access Sought

news.abstract: Suicide bomber blows himself up outside Shiite mosque in Baquba, Iraq, killing 4 other people and wounding 37; photos (M)
news.title: Suicide Bomber Outside Shiite Mosque in Iraq Kills Four Worshipers

news.abstract: Six South Korean politicians of different parties and SK Group chmn Son Kil Seung are arrested on charges in connection with widening inquiry into illegal campaign contributions and bribery; arrests are troubling to President Roh Moo Hyun, who entered office on pledge to fight corruption (M)
news.title: 7 Held in South Korean Scandal

news.abstract: Health officials expressed growing worry over the weekend about the possibility of another outbreak Chinas Guangdong Province.
news.title: 3rd Suspected SARS Case Emerges in China Province

news.abstract: Chief Warrant Officer Aaron A Weaver, 32, who survived famous Black Hawk Down attack in Somalia and, more recently, three rounds of surgery for testicular cancer, dies in Iraq in crash of Black Hawk helicopter near Falluja; Weaver, who relatives say insisted on serving in Iraq, dies with eight others while en route to medical checkup; photo; he was awarded Bronze Star in 1994 (M)
news.title: Survivor of Somalia and Cancer Dies on Doomed Copter in Iraq

news.abstract: Conditions at Apatit fertilizer factory in Arctic town of Kirovsk, Russia, reflect disruptions caused by post-Soviet society's tumultuous encounter with capitalism; few of Apatit's 14,000 workers want to stay, but even fewer have better options; production at factory lags far behind levels during Soviet era; Apatit is owned by jailed tycoon Mikhail B Khodorkovsky, who is charged with defaulting on payment in his 1994 acquisition of company, among other things; Khodorkovsky's defense points to massive capital investment in Apatit; photo (M)
news.title: In Post-U.S.S.R. Russia, Any Job Is a Good Job

news.abstract: American soldiers kill two Iraqi police officers and detain a third unidentified man in gun battle under confused circumstances in Kirkuk, where ethnic tensions have been rising between Kurds and local Arabs and Turkmen; Danish troops find dozens of buried mortar rounds that might contain blister gas, which Saddam Hussein has said he had destroyed; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Soldiers Kill 2 Members Of Iraqi Police

news.abstract: Jaime de Pinies, who was member of Spain's delegation to United Nations for 29 years and presided over 40th General Assembly in 1985, dies at age 86 (S)
news.title: Jaime de Piniés, 86, Spanish Envoy to U.N.

news.abstract: Pres Bush and 33 elected leaders of the Americas will meet in Monterrey, Mex, without common vision for future of Western Hemisphere; expectations for great progress are low and friction on important proposals are high (M)
news.title: Expectations Are Low for Progress at Americas Conference

news.abstract: Dr Rainer Hildebrandt, human rights activist and director of Museum dedicated to those who fled from Russian zone in Berlin during Cold War, dies at age 89; photo (M)
news.title: Rainer Hildebrandt, Museum Head, 89, At Berlin Crossing

news.abstract: United States Army has converted former Iraqi Republican Guard officers' club in Baghdad into little American oasis for war-weary soldiers; it now serves as First Armored Div's version of five-star hotel for as many as 100 soldiers at a time who are lucky enough to get three-day, two-night pass; more than 1,800 troops have cycled through since hotel opened in mid-Oct; amenities described; photo (M)
news.title: In the Center Of Baghdad, An Escape To America

news.abstract: The United States, in its hunt for terrorists, is creating chaos in the world of travel. Now a provincial judge is organizing the resistance.
news.title: An Eye for an Eye, a Tooth for a Tooth

news.abstract: Yusuf I Krymshamkhalov and Adam Dekkushev are convicted and sentenced to life in prison for 1999 bombing of three apartment buildings, in which 243 people were killed; critics of trial contend Russian secret service was involved in bombings, which took place in Moscow and Volgodonsk (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: 2 Get Life In Apartment Bombings

news.abstract: Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iran's supreme religious leader, says he will not intervene for moment in gathering confrontation between two main political camps in Iran--hard-liners and reformists--after review panel that he controls bars hundreds of reformist candidates from running in parliamentary elections next month; he meets with governors from around country who threaten to resign en masse if exclusions stand; he urges them to avoid tension; photo (M)
news.title: Iran Leader Delays Ruling On Exclusion Of Reformists

news.abstract: Two French journalists sentenced to six months in jail for traveling to Pakistani city of Quetta without government's permission are freed on appeal; Pakistani journalist working with them is missing and believed to be in government detention; Pakistani officials had accused journalists of staging film about resurgent Taliban in Quetta, but never formally charged them in relation to those accusations; under policy begun last year, Pakistan's Interior Ministry issues journalists restricted visas that bar them from traveling to Quetta, Peshawar and certain other spots without government permission (M)
news.title: Pakistani Judge Releases Pair Of Journalists

news.abstract: Swedish prosecutors charge Mijailo Mijailovic with murder of Foreign Minister Anna Lindh, who was stabbed last September; Mijailovic has confessed, but holds stabbing was not politically motivated (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Sweden: Murder Charge In Minister's Stabbing

news.abstract: Harold Shipman, the suburban doctor who won his patients trust before killing at least 215 of them, committed suicide in his prison cell today.
news.title: British Doctor Who Killed 215 Hangs Himself

news.abstract: Pres Bush gets skeptical response from other Western Hemisphere leaders when he argues at meeting in Monterrey, Mexico, that free trade is key to lifting tens of millions in hemisphere out of poverty; final declaration does not include 2005 deadline sought by Bush for Free Trade Area of the Americas, nor does it ban 'corrupt' governments from future meetings or adopt Bush's thinking that trade is best, most certain path to prosperity; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Meets Skepticism on Free Trade at Americas Conference

news.abstract: Iraq staggers through another day of violence and instability; guerrillas shoot down Apache helicopter in Habbaniya; two Iraqi civilians are killed by American soldiers who open fire during anti-Americans protest in Falluja; four relatives of Izzat Ibrahim al-Douri, Saddam Hussein's former vice president and the most wanted fugitive in Iraq, are arrested in Samarra; photos (M)
news.title: Army Copter Downed West of Baghdad in Hotbed of Anti-U.S. Sentiment

news.abstract: The confessed killer of Anna Lindh, Swedens foreign minister, denied today that he had intended to kill her but said he could not ignore voices in his head.
news.title: Killer of Swedens Foreign Minister Tells of Hearing Voices

news.abstract: World Health Organization confirms that two new cases of polio in Benin and Cameroon were spread from Nigeria; is concerned that Muslim leaders have suspended vaccination in parts of northern Nigeria (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Polio Spread From Nigeria, W.H.O. Confirms

news.abstract: Adoption of Constitution by Afghan loya jirga does not end lawlessness and human rights abuses that that prevail in provinces outside Kabul, especially in remote areas where self-appointed commanders reign; Afghan Human Rights Commission has recorded 1,700 complaints of violations from around country, including 225 accusations of murder involving commanders or other officials; photo (M)
news.title: Hurray! A Constitution! (Tell It to the Warlords)

news.abstract: Sen Edward Kennedy says Pres Bush has broken bond of trust with Americans, marketing Iraq like 'political product' to elect Republicans and reaping 'poison fruit of our misguided and arrogant foreign policy'; speech to Center for American Progress charges administration used fear after Sept 11 attacks to justify war of choice; singles out Vice Pres Cheney, Sec Donald Rumsfeld and Deputy Sec Paul Wolfowitz as 'axis of war' (M)
news.title: Kennedy Says War in Iraq Was Choice, Not Necessity

news.abstract: South Koreas foreign minister resigned today, accepting responsibility for a rift between pro-U.S. officials at his ministry and members of President Roh Moo Hyuns staff.
news.title: South Korea Aide Resigns in Rift Over U.S. Ties

news.abstract: Baghdad police bomb squad, which existed under Saddam Hussein but was far less active, defuses many more bombs each day than actually explode; photos (M)
news.title: Iraqi Team Disables Bombs With a Snip and a Prayer

news.abstract: Car bomb explodes outside police headquarters in Baquba, Iraq, killing driver and at least two bystanders and wounding 26 others, mostly policemen; Gen Mark Kimmitt announces capture of Khamis Sirhan al-Muhammad, 54 on US list of 55 most-wanted former officials; two Pakistanis and one Turk traveling with supply convoy are killed near Tikrit; 62 Bulgarian soldiers reportedly have left 480-member peacekeeping unit bound for Iraq; Francis J Ricciardone is named State Department director of policy on Iraq (M)
news.title: A Suicide Bomber Kills at Least 2 Iraqis at a Police Station Northeast of Baghdad

news.abstract: Pride of America, cruise ship, takes on water and tilts 15 degrees starboard during North Sea storm; first new oceangoing ship to fly United States flag in 50 years is still in final construction stage in Bremmerhaven (Germany) and accident is under investigation (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Rains Tilt U.S.-Flagged Cruise Ship

news.abstract: RUSSIA: Inquiry Into Pneumonia In Army; BRITAIN: Here Lies, There Goes;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Bush administration, hoping to rescue its troubled plan to restore sovereignty to Iraq, is joining Iraqi leaders to press United Nations to play role in choosing interim government in Baghdad; American administrator L Paul Bremer III and Iraqi delegation led by Adnan Pachachi, chairman of Iraqi Governing Council, will make urgent appeal for greater UN involvement; tens of thousands of demonstrators in Basra put pressure on US to support calls by leading Shiite cleric Grand Ayatollah Ali Al-Sistani for direct elections; new move at UN involves yet another change in strategy for administration under pressure from shifting events in Iraq; administration has had ambivalent attitude toward UN from very start of planning war to oust Saddam Hussein; it is also considering reversing itself and allowing businesses in countries that opposed war, including France, Germany and Russia, to bid on contracts to rebuild Iraq; photos (M)
news.title: U.S. JOINS IRAQIS TO SEEK U.N. ROLE IN INTERIM RULE

news.abstract: World Health Orgn official says three cases of SARS that have been identified in Guangzhou, China, so far this winter appear to be milder strain of disease, and public health system seems well prepared to prevent larger outbreak (S)
news.title: Fresh SARS Cases in China Called Milder

news.abstract: Prime Min Silvio Berlusconi of Italy has virtually disappeared from public view in last month; that and his reputation for cosmetic enhancement have prompted reports that he has undergone plastic surgery; he and his party face several political tests in coming months, and associate says he 'needs to look good'; photo (M)
news.title: Rome Journal; Is Berlusconi Remaking Himself With Eyes to the Future?

news.abstract: Hassan Rowhani, head of Iran's National Security Council, meets in Paris with French Foreign Min Dominque de Villepin, and two men clash over coming Iranian parliamentary elections and human rights; de Villepin uses blunt language unusual in diplomacy, demanding that Iran's elections next month be free and fair and that people arrested for their political beliefs be released; Rowhani strongly defends Iran's electoral process and rejects what he calls 'interference of any country' in Iran's internal affairs; Rowhani negotiated accord last Oct with de Villepin and his British and German counterparts that commits Iran to agree to more intrusive international inspections of its nuclear sites by International Atomic Energy Agency and suspension of its activities to enrich uranium; Rowhani insists his country is respecting its agreements, despite strong suspicions that Iran continues to assemble centrifuges that can be used to enrich uranium (M)
news.title: Political Barbs Welcome An Iranian Visiting France

news.abstract: Penicillin developer Dr Norman Heatley dies at age 92 (M)
news.title: Dr. Norman Heatley, 92, Dies; Pioneer in Penicillin Supply

news.abstract: Bush administration says Russia is hoping to leverage its plans for debt relief for Iraq to win revival of oil development projects signed under Saddam Hussein and suspended by occupation authorities (M)
news.title: Russia Sees Iraqi Debt Relief As Link to Oil, U.S. Aides Say

news.abstract: Defense Dept confirms death of one American service member in Iraq (S)
news.title: Names of the Dead

news.abstract: US law enforcement officials are trying to determine whether Pakistani government is involved in plot by South African businessman Asher Karni to export trigger devices that could be used for nuclear weapons; Karni, Israeli who lives in South Africa, was arrested in Denver in early Jan on charges that he illegally exported devices to Pakistan without license; is accused of ordering 200 trigger devices from PerkinElmer Optoelectronics of Salem, Mass (M)
news.title: U.S. Officials Try to Trace Illegal Sale of Nuclear Technology

news.abstract: BBC talk show host Robert Kilroy-Silk, who has been on air for 17 years, quits because of uproar surrounding anti-Arab comments he made in Sunday Express newspaper column; complaints were lodged by Muslim Council of Britain among other groups; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: TV Host Out After Arab Remarks

news.abstract: A court in the city of Seville has ruled that the owner of a so-called alternative club must make social security payments for 12 women who worked there as prostitutes.
news.title: Bordello Business Unsettled After Spanish Court Ruling

news.abstract: A large bomb exploded at the main gate of the American headquarters in Baghdad, killing and wounding people gathered nearby. Page 12.
news.title: Deadly Blast in Baghdad

news.abstract: Irish police evacuated all 147 people on board within 10 minutes and began interviewing passengers about a note saying a bomb was on board.
news.title: Flight to U.S. Lands in Ireland After Bomb Scare

news.abstract: Prince Alfonso Hohenlohe-Langenburg turned the Spanish fishing village of Marbella into a glittery jet-set playground.
news.title: Prince Alfonso Hohenlohe-Langenburg, Who Built Resorts, Dies at 79

news.abstract: The truck bomb, which exploded at the main gate of the American occupation headquarters, killed at least 20 people and wounded at least 60 others.
news.title: Blast in Baghdad Kills at Least 20 Outside U.S. Post

news.abstract: Achuar Indians, dominant tribe in Ecuadorean Amazon, help run Kapawi Ecolodge and Reserve, offering ecology-friendly getaways and jungle tours; for Achuar people, Kapawi is increasingly important symbol of their independence as they try to resist oil companies that want to drill there; their idea is to demonstrate options to oil exploration; photos; map (M)
news.title: Kapawi Journal; Ecuador Indians Fend Off Oil Companies With Tourism

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon says Israel might alter route of its separation barrier in West Bank, acknowledging that barrier has caused difficulties for ordinary Palestinians; says that in making alterations, his government would not be swayed by demands made by Palestinians, United Nations or International Court of Justice in The Hague; Israel says barrier is intended as security measure against suicide bombers and other Palestinian attacks; Palestinians say it amounts to confiscation of West Bank land they are demanding for future state; photo (M)
news.title: Sharon Hints Israel Might Alter Route of West Bank Barrier, but Not to Meet Outside Demands

news.abstract: Resort developer Prince Alfonso Hohenlohe-Lnagenburg dies at age 79; photo (M)
news.title: Prince Alfonso Hohenlohe-Langenburg, 79; Built Resorts

news.abstract: Dozens of people wounded in latest suicide bombing in Baghdad pour into hospitals, while relatives of those missing visit yard of city morgue; Iraqi insurgents are mounting their most spectacular attacks against Iraqis themselves; working for Americans makes Iraqi a traitor in eyes of insurgents, and viable target; in Iraq's ravaged economy, Americans are among few sources of steady pay; photo (M)
news.title: A Suicide Bombing Spreads Anguish Through the Working-Class Families of Baghdad

news.abstract: United Nations Secretary General Kofi Annan indicated that he would like to help but that further meetings were necessary.
news.title: U.N. Pressed to Send Team to Iraq to Aid Political Transition

news.abstract: The proposed French law prohibiting the wearing of religious symbols in public schools was expanded today to include bandannas worn by girls.
news.title: Next Target in the French Headgear Debate: The Bandanna

news.abstract: Lt Gen Thomas F Metz, who will soon take command of day-to-day military operations in Iraq, orders training for Army's III Corps for mission that goes far beyond usual tabletop war games and field exercises; headquarters staff of III Corps, at Fort Hood, Tex, drills with scenarios cast well into June for weather and religious holidays and local politics; Metz has assigned his commanders and senior noncommissioned officers reading list on Islam; knows his troops will be engaged in everything from firefights to fixing sewers; photo (M)
news.title: G.I.'s Headed for Iraq Train For Peace as Well as War

news.abstract: NORWAY: 2 Dead, 16 Missing As Freighter Capsizes; BRITAIN: Cases Of Infant Death To Be Reopened; IRELAND: Arrest In Plane Hoax; NORTHERN IRELAND: Power-Sharing Review; SWEDEN: Suspect In MinisterS Death Must Undergo Tests; FINLAND: Rigor Mortis On The Job;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Irish police arrest 19-year-old passenger on Delta airlines flight from Frankfurt (Germany) to Atlanta after bomb scare forces emergency landing in Shannon (Ireland); flight continues on to destination (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Ireland: Arrest In Plane Hoax

news.abstract: British Court of Appeal states it plans to halt all prosecution of deaths that could have been caused by sudden infant death syndrome and will review past convictions; 258 British adults have been convicted of killing child under age 2 and more than 50 are still in prison (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Cases Of Infant Death To Be Reopened

news.abstract: Iran's Guardian Council, which touched off storm by rejecting 3,600 candidates for parliament, backs off somewhat, reinstating 200 and announcing plans to approve more (S)
news.title: Top Iranian Council Reinstates 200 Parliamentary Candidates

news.abstract: Thousands of Iraqis demonstrate again in four major cities, demanding that US hand over Saddam Hussein to stand trial and renewing calls for direct elections; photo (S)
news.title: Iraqis Again Seek Elections and a Local Trial for Hussein

news.abstract: US military says raid in southern Afghanistan killed only five Taliban fighters, not 11 civilians as Afghan officials reported (S)
news.title: U.S. Says Only Taliban Died in Raid

news.abstract: Pres Vladimir Putin tells visiting World Bank head James D Wolfensohn that Russia wants to use its higher profile as Bank member to illustrate gains in economic and fiscal situation (S)
news.title: Putin Eager to Show Russian Gains In Meeting With World Bank Head

news.abstract: Rightwing paramilitaries are taking over Colombia's most fertile land, forcing farmers off or intimidating them into selling at low prices, even as government tries to wrest control of historically lawless country; photo; paramilitary leaders are negotiating with government while quietly laundering drug money by taking huge tracts from poor farmers and even big landowners (M)
news.title: Colombia's Landed Gentry: Coca Lords and Other Bullies

news.abstract: Agricultural officials in Hong Kong report that dead peregrine falcon found near two chicken farms there was infected with avian influenza virus, in first sign that disease may be present in China; it is spreading in chicken flocks in Vietnam, South Korea and Japan; World Health Orgn officials describe scale of spread as 'unprecedented' and warn that disease could evolve to spread from person to person, and not just from birds to people; Thailand and Laos have also reported large scale deaths of chickens in last several days and Thai officials say they are testing three people for possible bird flu; WHO has confirmed five cases in people in Vietnam, all of whom have died (M)
news.title: Dead Falcon in Hong Kong Found to Be Infected With Bird Flu

news.abstract: LIBYA: U.S. Lawmakers Plan Trip; EGYPT: Belly Ban Continues;.
news.title: World Briefing: Middle East

news.abstract: Pres Mohammad Khatami of Iran offers mixed message of hope and defiance to this year's World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland; says he hopes Iran's election will be free and competitive, but he leaves open question of his own future; he threatened to resign after country's conservative religious leaders disqualified 3,600 candidates for parliamentary elections; he rejects Bush administation's allegations that Iran is seeking nuclear weapons; notes his government allowed United Nations inspectors to tour Iran's nuclear facilities; also dismisses suggestion that he meet with Vice Pres Dick Cheney, who will deliver speech in Davos well after Khatami is supposed to return to Tehran; Khatami has threatened to resign before in clashes between his reform-minded government and Guardian Council (M)
news.title: Iran's Leader Mixes Hope With Defiance In Davos Talk

news.abstract: British government plans to eliminate anonymity for those who donate eggs and sperm after April 2005; plan needs Parliamentary approval (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Britain: Sperm Donors To Lose Anonymity

news.abstract: German army head Lt Gen Gert Gudera asks for early retirement; will be replaced by Hans-Otto Budde (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Germany: Army Chief Quits

news.abstract: European Commission reports sharp rise in number of Euro coin counterfiets in 2003; national banks detected only 2,339 fake coins in 2002, compared to 26,191 coins discovered in 2003 (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Euro Counterfeits On The Rise

news.abstract: RWANDA: Ex-Minister Gets Life In 1994 Genocide; IVORY COAST: Policeman Guilty Of Murder;.
news.title: World Briefing: Africa

news.abstract: Bush administration says it has teamed up with Saudi Arabia to freeze assets of four branches of major Islamic charitable foundation that they accuse of providing financial support to terrorist groups; single out branches in Kenya, Tanzania, Pakistan and Indonesia of Al-Haramain Charitable Foundation; Saudi officials say they have taken many steps to rein in charities that funnel money to Islamic terrorist groups, and they have ordered Al-Haramain to close all overseas branches; say they are not prepared to act against parent organization, which raises $50 million a year and finances legitimate charitable projects (M)
news.title: U.S. and Saudis Act to Freeze Charity's Assets

news.abstract: Second of three articles on expanding space race in developing world focuses on Brazil's unfulfilled space-age ambitions; country has tried three times to launch satellite on its own rocket; in most recent failure, in Aug, satellite rocket exploded on its launching pad, killing 21 scientists and technicians; that catastrophe provides vivid warning to other developing nations tempted to reach for grand ambitions in space on budgets already stretched thin by earthly needs; critics call such space programs vanity projects for poor nations still struggling to feed themselves; Brazilian officials, like those from India to China, describe their steadily expanding space effort as commercial and strategic necessity, as well as matter of national prestige; photos; map (L)
news.title: Brazil's Soaring Space-Age Ambitions Are Shy of Cash and Sapped by Calamity

news.abstract: Two Israeli cabinet ministers say Prime Min Ariel Sharon would have to resign if bribery investigation eventually leads to his indictment; indictment against developer David Appel does not lay out evidence that Sharon knowingly took bribe; Sharon's predecessors as prime minister Ehud Barak and Benjamin Netanyahu served under threat of indictments that never materialized, but they were distracted and sapped politically by long investigation; Sharon brushes off possibility of his indictment; public opinion polls suggest his personal credibility is shaky, and jockeying has begun within his Likud party to eventually succeed him; photo of Palestinian house in Nablus blown up by Israeli Army during standoff with wanted Palestinian militant, who is thought to have escaped (M)
news.title: Sharon Is Defiant in Face of Pressure Over Bribery Inquiry

news.abstract: Pakistan Pres Pervez Musharraf says scientists from his country appear to have sold nuclear designs to other nations; denies that government knew of sales; diplomats and US officials say documents recently obtained from Libya and Iran relating to their nuclear activities undercut years of Pakistani denials; believe that Pakistan received missile parts from North Korea in return for nuclear aid; International Atomic Energy Agency dir gen Mohamed ElBaradei comments; Musharraf photo (M)
news.title: Pakistan Chief Says It Appears Scientists Sold Nuclear Data

news.abstract: United Nations refugee agency is investigating reports that 18,000 Sudanese refugees, fleeing attacks on their villages, have crossed over into Chad; latest influx, adding to 95,000 Sudanese refugees already camped out near Chad-Sudan border, suggests that fighting in Sudanese region of Darfur continues to intensify, even as peace talks seek to end Sudan's other war, which has been going on for 20 years, between government in Khartoum and rebels in country's south; map (M)
news.title: Thousands of Refugees Reported to Be Fleeing Sudan for Chad

news.abstract: Last article in series The Next Space Race; India's national space program bills itself as thrifty space exploration for common man; India, with budget of only $450 million a year, has 13 satellites in orbit; it produces some of world's best remote imaging satellites and is planning to send satellite to moon by 2007 or 2008; only 6 of India's 37 satellite launchings have failed; engineers say they are using space technology to improve lives of tens of millions of Indians; say by using satellite imagery, they have helped 175 people in Majhgawan Karan reclaim 40 acres of barren land in area long haunted by hunger; photos (M)
news.title: India's Lofty Ambitions in Space Meet Earthly Realities

news.abstract: David Kay, who led US effort to find banned weapons in Iraq, says after stepping down from his post that he has concluded that Iraq had no stockpiles of chemical and biological weapons at start of war; says he thinks Iraq had illicit weapons at end of 1991 Persian Gulf war, but that United Nations inspections and Iraq's own decisions 'got rid of them'; CIA Dir George J Tenet names Charles A Duelfer to replace Kay; Duelfer photo (M)
news.title: IRAQ ILLICIT ARMS GONE BEFORE WAR, INSPECTOR STATES

news.abstract: VIENNA—  Before moving abroad, Alecia Myers and her husband Ken drove to Chicago to attend a daylong cross-cultural training seminar designed to teach them how to understand and relate to people from foreign cultures. There they learned about high context and low context cultures, sub-cultures, and co-cultures, the seven dimensions of culture, and increasing intercultural business competency. One year later, happily settled in Austria, Alecia looks back favorably on her cross-cultural training and tries to remember what she learned.
news.title: Cross-cultural training : How much difference does it really make?

news.abstract: Geo TV, Pakistani cable station transmitting from Dubai, is example of private television stations that are gaining favor over state-run media across South Asia; Pakistani Pres Pervez Musharraf reversed ban on private television stations in 2002, in part because many Pakistanis turned to Indian cable stations for news rather than state-run Pakistan Television; ban on Indian programming remains in place; private media ownership allows greater freedom in material transmitted; photos (M)
news.title: Pakistan TV: A New Look At the News

news.abstract: Israels high court today suspended for 30 days the states efforts to expel the Palestinian father of an Israeli soldier, pending a hearing on granting him the right to remain in Israel.
news.title: Expulsion of Israeli Soldiers Father Is Suspended

news.abstract: Israel and Hezbollah agree to prisoner exchange brokered by Germany; Israel will return more than 400 prisoners of various nationalities captured during its occupation of southern Lebanon, as well as remains of fighters killed there; Hezbollah will free kidnapped Israeli businessman Elhanan Tannenbaum and hand over remains of three dead Israelis; exchange has produced anguished debate in Israel, with government, public and families of missing Israelis expressing mixed feelings (M)
news.title: Israel Agrees To Free Arabs In a Swap With Militants

news.abstract: Five American soldiers and four Iraqis are killed and dozens of Iraqis are wounded in series of attacks by Iraqi insurgents; US and Iraqi forces continue to conduct series of aggressive raids, including 52 on Jan 23 alone, bringing in prisoners, bomb-making materials and documents associated with intelligence services of former regime; Brig Gen Mark Kimmitt says attacks are effort to delay advent of democracy in Iraq; photo; map (M)
news.title: 5 G.I.'s Are Killed in a Wave of Violence

news.abstract: Italian Prime Minister Silvio Berlusconi's Forza Italia party celebrates its 10th anniversary; news media's focus on Berlusconi amid rumors that he has undergone cosmetic surgery highlights political analysts' doubts about whether party has its own identity and future or is entirely dependent on Berlusconi for its face, voice and vigor; Forza Italia holds more seats in parliament than any other party, but some analysts say it has no ideological underpinning or direction (M)
news.title: Italian Leader And His Party Face Questions At Anniversary

news.abstract: Israel's high court suspends for 30 days state's efforts to expel Adel Hussein, Palestinian father of an Israeli soldier, pending hearing on granting him right to remain in Israel; Hussein has been living illegally in Israel for years while seeking permission to remain legally; his ex-wife and son, Israeli Jews, have been lobbying on his behalf; family's circumstances are being widely covered in Israel, and Hussein's lawyer says public pressure is helping (M)
news.title: Israeli Court Suspends Expulsion Of Soldier's Palestinian Father

news.abstract: Hezbollah leader Sheik Hassan Nasrallah makes rare public appearance in Beirut, Lebanon, to trumpet as a victory prisoner-exchange deal with Israel, in which 430 Palestinians, Lebanese and other Arab prisoners will be swapped for kidnapped Israeli businessman and three Israeli soldiers kidnapped along Lebanese border in 2000; Nasrallah holds out possibility that not all soldiers are dead, as Israelis assume; complicated deal is sealed after months of painstaking negotiations with German mediator; some in Israel call deal lopsided and say it could encourage more kidnappings; Prime Min Ariel Sharon defends deal but says it was not easy decision; he emphasizes importance of second phase of deal: that Hezbollah will give 'significant, proven and clear information' about fate of Capt Ron Arad, Israeli Air Force navigator shot down in Lebanon in 1986 and captured by Lebanese guerrillas; United States considers Hezbollah one of most potent terrorist organizations; photo (M)
news.title: Hezbollah Hails Trading Of Prisoners

news.abstract: David A Kay, recently resigned chief weapons inspector for CIA, says American intelligence agencies failed to recognize that Iraq had all but abandoned its efforts to produce large quantities of chemical or biological weapons after first Persian Gulf war in 1991; says they did not detect that Iraq's unconventional weapons programs were in state of disarray in recent years under increasingly erratic leadership of Saddam Hussein, and they did not know that Hussein insisted on self-directing projects that were not vetted by anyone else, allowing wily scientists to fake weapons programs and pocket money themselves; says Iraq did attempt to revive its efforts to develop nuclear weapons in 2000 and 2001, but never got as far toward making bomb as Iran and Libya did; says Baghdad was working to produce biological weapon using poison ricon until American invasion last Mar; says Tariq Aziz, former deputy prime minister, said after his capture that Hussein had become increasingly divorced from reality during last two years of his rule; Kay says CIA missed significance of chaos in Iraqi leadership; photo (L)
news.title: Ex-Inspector Says C.I.A. Missed Disarray in Iraqi Arms Program

news.abstract: To counter the threats made by Shiite leader Sistani, the Americans, at a loss, are now turning to the United Nations again. They want the UN to help bring peace to Iraq.
news.title: The Mullah and Democracy

news.abstract: Helmut Newton, the master photographer of sexual perversity and the founding father of androgynous imagery, died Friday at 83 in a way that he might have scripted in his narrative fashion photographs: from an accident in his Cadillac at Chateau Marmont, the star-studded Hollywood hotel. He was wintering there as usual, with his wife of 55 years, June, known as the photographer Alice Springs.
news.title: OBITUARY : Helmut Newton, master of the perverse image

news.abstract: White House backs away from assertions that Iraq had illegal weapons, saying administration wants to compare prewar intelligence assessments with what may be actually found; outgoing weapons inspector Dr David Kay's criticism of prewar intelligence increases pressure on CIA and intensifies debate on who shaped reports that Pres Bush used to justify invasion; White House stops asserting that weapons will eventually be found, although press secretary Scott McClellan says Bush was right to depose Saddam Hussein given his history; Kay reports scant evidence that Hussein had stockpiles of illicit weapons and says CIA under George Tenet was wrong in its contrary assessment (M)
news.title: White House Shows Less Certainty Now About Iraq's Arms

news.abstract: Gen Mirza Aslam Beg, former commander of Pakistan's army, says he never approved transfer of atomic information; senior nuclear scientists reportedly say Beg would have had to approve technology transfer to Iran; Beg says scientists should not be punished for selling nuclear technology and that Muslim countries should not give up pursuit of such weapons until India and Israel destroy arsenals; interview; photos; expresses deep antipathy to US (M)
news.title: General Denies Letting Secrets Of A-Bomb Out Of Pakistan

news.abstract: Prime Minister Tony Blair today avoided a political humiliation that threatened to bring down his government.
news.title: British Leader Narrowly Wins Key Vote

news.abstract: Olivier Guichard, guardian of France's Gaullist legacy and architect of its regional administration, dies at age 83; photo (M)
news.title: Olivier Guichard, 83, One of the Last Barons of Gaullism

news.abstract: Afghan President Hamid Karzai, at Kabul ceremony, signs Afghanistan's new Constitution into law; document was approved by loya jirga, grand council, on January 4; former King Mohammad Zahir Shah attends signing ceremony; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Afghanistan: Constitution Is Law

news.abstract: Prime Min Tony Blair narrowly defeats revolt in his Labor Party, winning passage, 316-311, of bill to revamp Britain's higher education system and avoiding political humiliation that threatened to bring down his government; bill will require university students, who now make only nominal tuition payments, to begin paying up to $5,500 a year starting in 2006; existing tuition, which is means-tested and paid by fewer than half of students, was put in place by Blair in 1998 and has been object of protests; opposition Conservatives have called for complete tuition rollback (M)
news.title: Blair Narrowly Prevails in a Vote to Raise Tuition Fees

news.abstract: Senegal, long dominated by France, is marching headlong into United States camp now that war on terrorism has spurred US interest in Africa; responds to number of factors, including drop in French aid; France remains biggest donor and trade partner, but Senegal's relations with US have already strained its ties with France; map; photo (M)
news.title: America Tugs at French-Accented Lands: It's Not Peanuts

news.abstract: State Sec Colin L Powell seeks to assure Russians that United States has no intention of encircling or threatening Russia despite American plans to redeploy some troops to former Soviet bloc nations in Eastern Europe, Moscow radio interview; says American forces in Europe are falling from over 300,000 to under 100,000; notes Pres Bush weighs putting 'temporary facilities' in Eastern Europe for training or use as air bases; says he got assurances from Pres Vladimir V Putin that charges against Mikhail B Khodorkovsky will be fully explained and that his trial will be open; says US has no intention of expelling Russia from Group of 8 industrial nations because of case; cites need to exercise restraint in war with Chechen separatists in accordance with human rights norms; dismisses idea that US-Russia ties are chilling or that Russian democracy is in danger (M)
news.title: Powell Seeks to Reassure Russians on New Troops

news.abstract: Russia places 10 Yukos Oil shareholders or employees on international wanted lists, including some senior executives who have sought asylum in Israel; move suggests prosecution of Yukos is extending far beyond former chief executive Mikhail B Kodorkovsky and his partner, Platon Lebedev, who are both in jail; Russia names three of those sought, Leonid B Nevzlin, Mikhail B Brudno and Vladimir M Dubov, all of whom are in Israel; Moscow court rejects Khodorkovsky's challenge of his Oct arrest (M)
news.title: Russia Issues International Wanted List in Oil Case

news.abstract: At least 25 people have been killed in drug related violence across Mexico including federal drug agents and former Deputy State Attorney General (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Wave Of Killings

news.abstract: The BBCs director general resigned today, saying that he hoped his departure would staunch the damage from a devastating report.
news.title: Second Top BBC Executive Quits; Blair Accepts Apology

news.abstract: Long-awaited report by Lord Hutton, senior British judge, clears Prime Min Tony Blair and his government of any deliberate attempt to deceive public on threat from Iraq mentioned in Sept 2002 intelligence dossier; castigates BBC for sloppy, inaccurate reporting and 'defective' editorial supervision in asserting that Blair and aides exaggerated case for war; Lord Hutton reads conclusions from bench in Royal Courts of Justice; photos; BBC chairman Gavyn Davies later resigns in one of worst debacles in famous network's history; findings are personal vindication for Blair, beleaguered by rebellion within Labor Party; BBC editor-in-chief Greg Dyke issues recorded statement saying broadcaster Andrew Gilligan has already admitted that 'certain key allegations' were wrong; defends right to reveal concerns of Dr David Kelly, weapons scientist who was Gilligan's source; Kelly's suicide last July set off uproar; Blair, in Parliament, indignantly demands apology (M)
news.title: Report on Iraq Case Clears Blair and Faults BBC

news.abstract: The cause of one of the single most-deadly incidents involving U.S. forces in Afghanistan since the war remained unclear.
news.title: Explosion in Afghanistan Kills 7 U.S. Soldiers and Injures 3

news.abstract: French cabinet approves draft law prohibiting wearing of religious symbols, including Islamic head scarves, in public schools; bill, supported by President Jacques Chirac, must be approved by National Assembly to become law (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: France: Cabinet Backs Rule Against Scarves

news.abstract: PHILIPPINES: Executions Stayed; CHINA: Sect Sues Minister;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: United Nations official reports that Sudanese plane bombed border town in Chad as part of effort to quell year-long western Darfur area insurgency; 2 civilians and 15 others are killed (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Sudan: Plane Bombs Chad Side Of Border

news.abstract: In a blow to President Jacques Chirac, the former prime minister Alain Juppé was found guilty today of illegal party financing.
news.title: French Court Finds Ex-Minister Guilty of Illegal Party Funding

news.abstract: Taiwan, protesting French President Jacques Chirac's criticism of island's planned missile defense referendum, will break off high-level government exchanges with France (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Taiwan: Rebuke To Chirac

news.abstract: GERMANY: 9/11 Prisoner Seeks Retrial; BRITAIN: Marijuana Laws Relaxed; BRITAIN: Couple Out Over Puppy Farming;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Sec of State Colin L Powell, meeting with Turkish Prime Min Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Washington, offers assurances that Kurds in a newly soverign Iraq will have to relinquish their control of oil resources in north; Turkish officials say they remain concerned that United States may still yield to Kurdish demands for autonomous state; photo (M)
news.title: Turkey, Seeking U.S. Pledge on the Kurds' Role in the New Iraq, Finds Mixed Message

news.abstract: Iraqi authorities, with help of US intelligence agencies, are creating intelligence service that will focus on rooting out guerrilla fighters, especially those from outside country; service will employ some former agents of Saddam Hussein's security apparatus and will probably receive financing from US; it will employ 500 to 2,000 people, and is expected to be formed before Bush administration transfers sovereignty to Iraqi government on June 30; CIA is taking lead in helping put together new service; photo shows partly destroyed headquarters of Saddam Hussein's secret police (M)
news.title: NEW IRAQ AGENCY TO HUNT REBELS

news.abstract: Andrew Gilligan, reporter at center of dispute between British Broadcasting Corp and British government over whether government had exaggerated case for war against Iraq, resigns from BBC; follows BBC chmn Gavyn Davies and dir gen Greg Dyke, who left their posts after scathing official report that accused Gilligan of sloppy reporting and his employers of host of journalistic and management failures (M)
news.title: Reporter at Center of Dispute Over Iraq Resigns From BBC

news.abstract: Canadian Supreme Court rules that parents can spank their children but decision limits use of punishment to children over age 2 and under age 12 and charges parents to control degree of force applied (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Canada: Court Backs Spanking

news.abstract: Mexican Attorney General names special prosecutor to investigate unsolved murders of at least 300 women in Ciudad Juarez over past ten years (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Mexico: Prosecutor For Unexplained Killings

news.abstract: SERBIA: Close, But No Speaker Vote; GERMANY: 9/11 Suspect Called A Codes Expert; GERMANY: SchrÖDer To Visit White House; ROMANIA: Candidate Seeks A New Image; RUSSIA: U.S. Fails On Agreement For Weapons Raids; THE NETHERLANDS: Support For Arms To China; BELGIUM: Minister Chided For U.S. Criticism;.
news.title: World Briefing: Europe

news.abstract: Dr Omar Abdulcadir of Florence, Italy, treats African victims of female genital cutting; has asked local health officials for permission to perform less severe and largely symbolic operation under hospital conditions to lessen pain and risks of infection; issue is part of larger debate on rights of Europe's immigrant community to continue traditional practices; those who cling to tradition either take their daughters to Africa for procedure or have it done illegally in Europe; photo (M)
news.title: Doctor in Italy Tries to Ease Pain of an African Tradition

news.abstract: Pakistani government removes scientist Abdul Qadeer Khan, founder of country's nuclear weapons program, from post as special adviser to prime minister; Khan and other scientists and military officers are implicated in illicit sale of nuclear technology to Iran, Libya and other countries; it is not clear whether Khan or others will be prosecuted; Pakistani Pres Pervez Musharraf has been under competing pressures from United States, secular and Islamic political rivals and politically powerful army in pursuing investigation; photo (M)
news.title: Pakistan Ousts Nuclear Scientist From Post

news.abstract: Secretary of State Colin L Powell's warnings to United Nations Security Council one year ago about Iraq's banned weapons programs have not been borne out by findings of Iraq Survey Group; his carefully worded presentation was considered Bush administration's most comprehensive public case about urgent threat Iraq posed to world; his reputation for caution and care gave it added credibility; now Dr David A Kay, Washington's chief weapons inspector as head of Iraq Survey Group, says Iraq had no significant stockpiles of chemical or biological weapons when invasion began in March; Washington is seized by question of how and why such an intelligence gap happened; interviews with intelligence officials, Iraqi engineers and others suggest that Powell's case was largely based on limited, fragmentary and mostly circumstantial evidence, with conclusions drawn on basis of little challenged assumption that Saddam Hussein would never dismantle old illicit weapons and would pursue new ones to fullest extent possible; photos; excerpts from Powell's Feb 2003 speech at UN and from Kay's recent testimony and interviews; drawings; map (L)
news.title: Powell's Case, a Year Later: Gaps in Picture of Iraq Arms

news.abstract: Yukihiko Ikeda, a longtime political figure in Japan, led his countrys efforts to resolve the 1990s hostage crisis in Peru.
news.title: Yukihiko Ikeda, 66, Japanese Lawmaker

news.abstract: Twelve people die in two bomb attacks in northern Iraq; suicide bomber attacks police station in Mosul, killing at least nine people and wounding 45; three American soldiers are killed when bomb destroys their Humvee in Kirkuk; Iraqi officials fear there could be more violence during visit next week by UN team to assess feasibility of holding elections in June; photo (M)
news.title: 3 G.I.'s Among 12 Killed in Bombings in Iraq

news.abstract: Two suicide bombers kill at least 56 people and wound at least 200, Erbil, during Muslim holiday fetes at separate headquarters of Iraq's two leading Kurdish political parties; blasts shatter calm of north, part of Iraq that had been relatively stable under American occupation; blasts, 10 minutes apart, kill several top leaders and wound other senior officials; come as two parties have been trying to unite region's divided administrations to strengthen demands to retain area's autonomy; American military officials, while expecting increase of violence during holiday, say there was little preparation to guard against suicide bombers; some officials suspect foreign fighters or Ansar al-Islam, mostly Kurdish terrorist group that may have ties to Al Qaeda, were involved in bombing; photos (M)
news.title: 56 KURDS KILLED IN SUICIDE BLASTS IN NORTH OF IRAQ

news.abstract: Dr Abdul Qadeer Khan, founder of Pakistan's nuclear arms program, reportedly has confessed that during last 15 years he has provided Iran, North Korea and Libya with designs and technology to produce fuel for nuclear weapons; senior Pakistani officials give Pakistani journalist exhaustive and startling account of how Khan, national hero, spread secret technology; say he presided over network that smuggled hardware, shared secret designs and gave personal briefings to Iranian, Libyan and North Korean scientists in covert meetings abroad in what he called effort to ease Western attention on Pakistan and help Muslim cause; carefully avoid pinning any blame on Pres Pervez Musharraf, army or Pakistani intelligence service, despite fact that some of material apparently was transported on government cargo planes; say all transfers ceased in early 2002; United States believes transfers to Libya continued through fall of 2003; it is unclear whether Khan, whose house has been surrounded by security officials for weeks, will be arrested; photo (M)
news.title: Key Pakistani Is Said to Admit Atom Transfers

news.abstract: Serbian ultranationalist and warlord Vojislav Seselj, known for his rabble-rousing speeches and foul language, has brought those habits to Hague, where he faces charges involving war crimes in Bosnia and Croatia in 1990s; sneers at United Nations court as American tool against Serbs and demands judges be disqualified; some court officials wonder how such an obstructionist defendant can get proper and fair trial; he is conducting own defense, which allows him to hold floor in court, even now at preparatory hearings; photo (M)
news.title: Hague Journal; Another Serb Defendant Stays on His Best Bad Behavior

news.abstract: Pres Bush plans to set up bipartisan panel to examine American intelligence operations, including study of possible misjudgment about Iraq's unconventional weapons; panel will also probe failures to penetrate secretive governments and stateless groups that could attempt new attacks on United States; decision follows rising pressure from both Democrats and many ranking Republicans to deal with errors that overstated Iraq's stockpiles of chemical and biological weapons and its progress toward developing nuclear arms; administration officials describe plans for broader examination of intelligence shortcomings to retool intelligence-gathering for new era of terrorism and nuclear proliferation by rouge scientists and nations that may provide arms for groups like Al Qaeda; panel will not report back until well after Nov elections (M)
news.title: BUSH TO ESTABLISH PANEL TO EXAMINE U.S. INTELLIGENCE

news.abstract: Intelligence officials have reluctantly begun to admit that major overhaul could be in order in wake of their failure to anticipate Sept 11 terrorist attacks and misjudgment of Iraq's arms stockpiles; hope independent panel Pres Bush will appoint can offer them more help and less finger pointing; have often derided recommendations of such panels as naive or unworkable; are least upset by Rep Porter J Goss's stand that any new inquiry should look forward, rather than dwell on past mistakes; Sen John D Rockefeller IV and others want inquiry to take Bush administration to task for building what they call flawed case that United States needed to act quickly against Iraq (M)
news.title: An Inquiry That's Awash In Disputes at the Outset

news.abstract: French Pres Jacques Chirac passionately defends Alain Juppe, his former prime minister and longtime political partner, who was convicted in corruption scandal dating from days when Chirac was Paris Mayor; others in Chirac's cabinent, including Prime Min Jean-Pierre Raffarin and Min Dominique de Villepin, earlier lauded Juppe; Magistrates' Union scores comments as threat to separation of powers; government probes obstruction of justice charges in case brought by Judge Catherine Pierce; photo (M)
news.title: Chirac Backs Longtime Ally Now Guilty Of Corruption

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon, outraging members of settlement movement he helped create, says he might seek to evacuate almost all Israeli settlers from Gaza Strip, newspaper interview; move is part of 'unilateral disengagement' from Palestinians he plans should Bush administration's peace plan fail; says he ordered plans for evacuation of 17 of at least 20 settlements; his aide says option is most far-reaching of three he will submit to cabinet; opponents on right and skeptics on left charge he seeks to divert attention from bribery scandal; settlers warn of political action to bring down his government; far-right parties do not immediately bolt from his governing coalition; Palestinians suspect public relations ploy; photos (M)
news.title: Angering Settlers, Sharon Says Most May Have to Leave Gaza

news.abstract: Deputy Sec Paul D Wolfowitz, on mission to highlight successes in Iraq, attends Kirkuk town council meeting and hears of ethnic and religious tensions that are vastly complicating American efforts for orderly turnover of sovereignty; holds all Iraq was Saddam Hussein's victim and that all Iraqis have equal stake in cooperating to build new and democratic nation; Maj Gen Raymond T Odierno addresses objections of Shiites and other groups to caucus system planned by United States to select initial new government (M)
news.title: Wolfowitz Gets an Earful on Ethnic Tensions

news.abstract: NEPAL: Protesters Injured; VIETNAM: Pirates Attack;.
news.title: World Briefing: Asia

news.abstract: National Indian Federation leader Patricia Gualinga reports failure of assassination attempt on federation head Leonidas Iza; Iza is unharmed, but three relatives, including his son, are injured; group opposes free-market reforms proposed by President Lucio Gutierrez; photo (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Ecuador: Indian Leader Attacked

news.abstract: Palestinian observer mission head Nasser al-Kidwa criticizes Israeli ambassador to United Nations Dan Gillerman for his recent comments faulting UN Sec Gen Kofi Annan's response to Jerusalem suicide bombing (S)
news.title: World Briefing | United Nations: Palestinian Criticizes Israeli Envoy

news.abstract: Prime Minister Tony Blair said today that freedom and democracy in Iraq were more important than any mistaken intelligence.
news.title: Blair Fields Criticism, and Heckling, as He Defends War

news.abstract: Defense Secretary Donald H. Rumsfeld told a Senate committee that weapons of mass destruction might yet be found in Iraq.
news.title: Rumsfeld Defends U.S. Intelligence Operations

news.abstract: Pres Bush presses United Nations Sec Gen Kofi Annan at White House meeting to have his aides mediate among quarreling factions in Iraq and forge consensus behind plan that would allow transfer of sovereignty to Iraqi government by June 30; Bush aides say Bush, without rapid progress on political issues, might agree to delay self-rule as last resort; Bush offers Annan dozen transfer options, ranging from holding direct elections before June 30 to radically overhauling unwieldy caucus system that is supposed to choose new national assembly; Annan, after meeting, says UN team heading soon to Iraq to assess possibility of direct elections will expand its agenda; says UN has chance to help break impasse; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Presses U.N. to Mediate Iraqi Clash on Rule

news.abstract: Prime Min Jean-Pierre Raffarin opens debate in French legislature on bill banning religious symbols in public schools; holds Muslim head scarves must be banned because they undermine republican ideal of freedom and equality; calls on Muslims to behave like good citizens; bill has divided cabinet and enraged Muslim minority, while heartening both Muslim and non-Muslim feminist groups; photo (M)
news.title: Debate Begins In France On Religion In the Schools

news.abstract: Secretary General Kofi Annan has invited Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders to New York next Tuesday.
news.title: U.N. Leader to Hold Talking on Reuniting Cyprus

news.abstract: As written, bill could allow President Putin to run for two new terms, conceivably keeping him in power until 2018.
news.title: Russia Considers Extending Presidential Term to 7 Years

news.abstract: Iran's supreme religious leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei seeks to resolve confrontation between reformist supporters of Pres Mohammad Khatami's government and their hard-line opponents; orders review of disqualifications of thousands of parliamentary candidates (S)
news.title: Iran's Supreme Leader Tries to Defuse Crisis

news.abstract: Treatise on family presented by Spanish Roman Catholic Bishops Conference causes uproar from women's rights groups and politicians; holds domestic violence is negative consequence of sexual liberation for women (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Spain: Outcry As Bishops Tie Battering To Sex

news.abstract: The leader of the Conservative Party of Britain, Michael Howard, called on Prime Minister Tony Blair today to resign.
news.title: Tory Leader Calls on Blair to Quit for Iraqi Weapons Claim
