news.abstract: Israeli armored bulldozers reinforced by helicopter gunships advance into Rafah refugee camp in southern Gaza Strip after Israeli troops seal camp off for what army calls large-scale operation to root out militants and weapons-smuggling tunnels; frightened Palestinians flee camp as troops and tanks draw cordon around it; other residents of camp pick through wreckage of dozens of homes smashed by Israeli forces during fierce fighting last week; raid follows killings last week of 13 Israeli soldiers in Gaza, including seven in Rafah area, and 32 Palestinians; national security adviser Condoleezza Rice offers mild criticism of Israel's demolition plan in Rafah, but European Union foreign ministers condemn action and UN Secretary General Kofi Annan appeals to Israeli government to stop destruction; photo (M)
news.title: Israeli Army Moves on Rafah Refugee Camp in Gaza

news.abstract: More than 7,000 Americans who died in Italy in World War II are buried in cemetery in Nettuno, near Rome; each lies buried with marble headstone that is cleaned twice a year, by hand, with pumice stone and soap; grounds are lovingly cared for; gratitude felt for Americans there is palpable, even after all these years; photo; map (M)
news.title: Nettuno Journal; A Tiny Corner of Italy That Hasn't Forgotten America

news.abstract: King Abdullah II of Jordan, key player in American diplomacy in Middle East, says that after US hands over formal sovereignty to Iraqis on June 30, country should be run by strongman--possibly drawn from ranks of Saddam Hussein's army, interview; seems to be registering disapproval of former Iraqi exiles at core of current leadership; says although Iraq's military elite was made up of Hussein loyalists, some older officers might not be tainted in same way as those on America's wanted list; king's remarks seem to run counter to American insistence on ridding Iraqi public of of former elite, but they reflect his growing concern that Iraq is heading for deeper strife, possibly civil war, before elections planned for next Jan; speaking of Israeli-Palestinian conflict, king suggests that Yasir Arafat should yield authority, demand rarely voiced so openly in Arab world; Jordan is in complicated position because majority of its people are of Palestinian descent; Abdullah must balance his close alliance with US and emotions of population increasingly hostile to American policy (M)
news.title: Old Iraq Army Could Provide A Leader, Jordan's King Says

news.abstract: More than 100 gang members in severely overcrowded prison in San Pedro Sula, Honduras, die in early-morning fire apparently caused by electrical short circuit; this is second major prison disaster in country in 13 months; 68 people died in Apr 2003 in ramshackle jail at El Porvenir, 51 of them executed by state police, soldiers, guards and prisoners working as trusties; no evidence available suggests foul play in fire, but in both disasters almost all of dead are members of violent youth gang that has created contining law enforcement crisis in country; photo (M)
news.title: At Least 100 Are Killed In Prison Fire In Honduras

news.abstract: AIDS activists and doctors who treat patients in poor countries greet Bush administration's shift in its policy on procuring AIDS drugs with mixed reviews; many are delighted, but some express frustration that White House has set up new approval process overseen by Food and Drug Administration when one overseen by World Health Orgn already exists; they consider this another roadblock (M)
news.title: Views Mixed On U.S. Shift On Drugs For AIDS

news.abstract: Canadian government proposes to allow women to obtain 'morning-after' birth control pill without prescription at any pharmacy (S)
news.title: Morning-After Pill in Canada: Prescription May Not Be Needed

news.abstract: Sonia Gandhi, Italian-born widow and daughter-in-law of slain prime ministers, stuns India by announcing she will 'humbly decline' to be prime minister, saying that has never been her aim in leading Congress Party to election victory over Hindu nationalist party; announcement sets off protests as emotional as those of Hindu nationalists who object to her foreign birth; photo; stock market rallies after plummeting over fears that Congress Party will reverse economic reforms; Gandhi reportedly favors Manmohan Singh, respected former finance minister, to lead country; adviser says she never wanted to be prime minister and entered politics in 1998 to defeat Hindu nationalists she viewed as threat to secular state (M)
news.title: GANDHI DECLINES TOP POST IN INDIA

news.abstract: Fellow civilian guards at Buckingham Correctional Center in rural Virginia defend Staff Sgt Ivan L Frederick II, accused of being central figure in abuse of prisoners at Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq; map (S)
news.title: Fellow Civilian Prison Guards Defend an Accused Sergeant

news.abstract: Military lawyers, who had active role in supervising interrogations in first Gulf War, have been excluded in Iraq, which human rights lawyer Scott Horton says may have played role in abuse of detainees at Abu Ghraib prison; photo; he and other attorneys say exclusion of Judge Advocate General's Corps suggests lack of concern with legal standards by Bush administration (M)
news.title: U.S. Barred Legal Review Of Detentions, Lawyer Says

news.abstract: Palestinians called it an unprovoked attack; Israeli military officials said there were gunmen in the crowd.
news.title: Israeli Shells Hit Crowd of Palestinians, Killing at Least 9

news.abstract: Bush administration is considering plan to allow Iraqi security forces to decline to take part in military operations ordered by American commanders, in response to concerns at United Nations about limitations on Iraq's future sovereignty; officials hope so-called 'opt-out' arrangement will help win support at Security Council for resolution conferring legitimacy on caretaker government to be installed in Iraq after June 30; photo (M)
news.title: White House Considers Plan to Let Iraqi Forces Opt Out of Military Operations Ordered by the U.S.

news.abstract: Pedophilia case that has captivated France, and destroyed lives of dozen people, collapses when main suspect, Myriam Delay, suddenly admits that she made up much of story; on 10th day of her trial, she tells stunned courtroom that her tale of gang rapes and child prostitution ring based in her home in Outreau was elaborate lie; points out several of accused, saying they are innocent; trial has shattered lives of 18 people accused in case, with one committing suicide and others losing custody of their children; Delay could face up to 2 years in jail for her false accusations, in addition to possible sentence of 20 years for sexual abuse of minors (M)
news.title: French Pedophilia Case Falls Apart When Main Suspect Recants

news.abstract: Two top commanders of American forces in Iraq, testifying before Senate Armed Services Committee, say Red Cross reports of prisoner abuse last year at Abu Ghraib prison did not reach them for months after complaints were submitted to their subordinates; Lt Gen Ricardo S Sanchez says he has ordered that Red Cross reports now be shown to senior commanders as soon as they are received; Gen John P Abizaid says he did not learn of broader report Red Cross submittedin Feb until early May; referring to way Red Cross reports are handled by military, he says 'system is broken'; Abizaid says preliminary inquiry by Army inspector general found problems with training, organization and doctine regarding military detention centers in Iraq and Afghanistan, but no 'pattern of abuse' of prisoners in Central Command's area of responsibility; photo (M)
news.title: Two U.S. Generals Outline a Lag in Notification on Reports of Abuse in Iraqi Prison

news.title: Top Arafat Aide Convicted by Israelis on Murder Charges

news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Greece: Bomb Alert At American School

news.abstract: Malawi parliamentary elections, which are nation's third democratic elections since ending three decades of dictatorship in 1994, draw large number of voters; President Bakili Muluzi is retiring after 10 years as leader and new Parliament will choose his successor (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Africa: Malawi: Vote For A New Leader

news.abstract: NATO has cast its decision to send forces to help stabilize Afghanistan as a vital step in its struggle for relevance.
news.title: NATO Flirts With Failure in Afghanistan

news.abstract: Chinese government denies government jobs to those who do not meet often unwritten code of fitness--height, looks and robust good health--that many say has nothing to do with their ability to perform task in question; standards are sign of how far China has drifted from Communist Party's stated socialist values; officials are no longer selected on basis of ideological fervor or working-class background, but rather in ways that seem more reminiscent of China's imperial history; rigorous requirements for height and physique have long been used to screen people who want to work in China's most internationally visible jobs; new effort to extend those standards to all government jobs is traced to China's effort to put best face forward since joining World Trade Orgn and interacting more with outside world; photo; map (M)
news.title: Chinese People's Republic Is Unfair to Its Short People

news.abstract: Chechen officials announce Aug 29 election to determine successor to Akhmad Kadyrov, who was recently killed in Grozny bomb attack; pro-Moscow Prime Minister Sergei B Abramov is acting president (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Chechnya Sets Election Date

news.abstract: Joint Chiefs of Staff Chmn Richard B Myers approves new national military strategy that makes clear to nation's war planners that they must pay greater attention to preparing for complicated and dangerous transition between end of major combat operations and return of civil authority in Iraq (M)
news.title: A New Strategy Document Calls Attention to the Transition Between War and Peace

news.abstract: Army Specialist Joseph M Darby says he told investigators about mistreatment of Iraqi prisoners at Abu Ghraib after he decided that it was 'morally wrong'; Darby stands out from other soldiers who learned of abuse; some soldiers say they tried to report misconduct or stop it, but nothing came of their efforts; Darby's report would initiate investigation into mistreatment of prisoners at Abu Ghraib and other military facilities in Iraq and raise questions about whether abuse was authorized by military officials; seven soldiers charged in investigation are all from Darby's unit, 372nd Military Police Co; Staff Sgt Ivan L Frederick II is described as ringleader of misconduct; Darby photo (M)
news.title: Only a Few Spoke Up on Abuse As Many Soldiers Stayed Silent

news.abstract: Five Afghans are killed and four US soldiers are wounded in clashes in Afghanistan; Pakistani officials protest what they say was second incursion by US forces into Pakistan in month (M)
news.title: 5 Afghans Die and 4 U.S. Soldiers Are Wounded in Clashes

news.abstract: Defense Dept officials are preparing for influx of compensation claims stemming from charges of abuse at Abu Ghraib prison in Iraq (M)
news.title: U.S. Preparing for Influx of Compensation Claims by Abused Iraqis

news.abstract: Libyan leader Col Muammar el-Qaddafi walks out of summit meeting of Arab leaders in Tunis; Qaddafi has repeatedly called for dismantling of Arab League and had to be coaxed to attend meeting; announces he is withdrawing from meeting because entire agenda is flawed; says Arab governments and Arab people have different agendas; Qaddafi's outbursts, while erratic, often reflect popular sentiment; latest move appears to reflect general Arab frustration over occupation of Iraq; photo (M)
news.title: Qaddafi Stalks Out of an Arab Assembly

news.abstract:  In Baghdad, a car bomb outside the home of an Iraqi deputy interior minister, Abdul-Jabbar Youssef al-Sheikhli, wounded him and killed at least five people  four security guards and a passer-by.
news.title: IRAQ UPDATE

news.abstract: A 120-foot section of a new terminal at Paris' Charles de Gaulle airport collapsed early Sunday, killing at least five people.
news.title: Roof Collapses at Paris Airport, Killing 5

news.abstract: Sums being offered on black market for sale of kidneys for transplant seem like fortune to people mired in poverty; in parts of Brazil where monthly wage is barely $80, giving up kidney for $6,000 represents huge opportunity--more than decade's wages; donors and recipients are linked by trafficking ring that authorities say exploits two very different needs: for money and for life itself; journey of kidney sold by Alberty Jose da Silva of Recife, Brazil, to American woman in Brooklyn, NY, by way of intermediary in Israel and surgery in South African hospital traced; final cost to recipient is $60,000; da Silva and other Brazilian kidney donors have seen their payments jeopardized when they were arrested and briefly jailed on suspicion of violating laws against trading in human organs; photos; map (L)
news.title: THE ORGAN TRADE: A Global Black Market; Tracking the Sale of a Kidney On a Path of Poverty and Hope

news.abstract: Cannes Film Festival awards Palm d'Or to Michael Moore's movie Fahrenheit 9/11; movie, highly critical of Bush administration's foreign policies, particularly war in Iraq, is one of only three non-fiction films allowed in competition in nearly 50 years; Moore, who says he did not set out to make political film, is still looking for American distributor for movie (M)
news.title: Moore's 'Fahrenheit 9/11' Wins Top Honors at Cannes

news.abstract: PARIS:—  At the heart of the European Commission's review of the proposed merger of Sony Music and BMG, the recording company owned by Bertelsmann, is the search for a satisfactory response to one question: Where do music prices come from?
news.title: Impact of Sony-BMG merger is at issue : EU is taking a long look at puzzling cost of music

news.abstract: Brig Gen Janis Karpinski, former head of military police at Abu Ghraib, says Lt Gen Ricardo S Sanchez, top American general in Iraq, rejected her recommendation in Jan that military make public Arabic-language radio or television address to Iraqi people to confront accusations of abuse at prison; says Sanchez visited military intelligence unit at Abu Ghraib at least three times in Oct, when first of worst of abuses were taking place; Sanchez has said he did not learn of abuses until Jan 14, but Karpinski says that in late Nov, Sanchez's top deputy Maj Gen Walter Wojdakowski was present at meeting at which there was extensive discussion of Red Cross report that cited specific cases of abuse; two Defense Dept offiicals acknowledge that command in Baghdad was reluctant to say too much at outset because of continuing criminal investigation; photos (M)
news.title: General Says Sanchez Rejected Her Offer to Give Address to Iraqis About Abuses

news.abstract: Chinese Baseball League All-Stars, China's first professional baseball league, is in its second season; few fans turn out and players lack skills, but promoters are optimistic; country is gearing up to host 2008 Olympics in Beijing, where it will compete in sport for first time; photo (M)
news.title: Beijing Journal; China Warms Up and Practices for a Future in Baseball

news.abstract: Investigators are checking whether U.S. officials gave secrets to Ahmad Chalabi, the Iraqi suspected of passing them to Iran. Page A11.
news.title: Inquiry on Secrets

news.abstract: Excerpts from Pres Bush's speech on American strategy in Iraq (M)
news.title: Excerpts From Bush Speech on American Strategy in Iraq

news.abstract: Central Intelligence Agency's practice of keeping some detainees in Abu Ghraib prison off official rosters so concerned top Army officer and civilian official there that they reached written agreement early this year to stop; undated memorandum is described as agreement between Army intelligence unit assigned to prison and 'external agencies,' euphemism for CIA, to halt practices that bypass both military rules and international standards; Maj Gen Antonio M Taguba, Army officer who first investigated prison abuses, complained that military guards were being enlisted to hide prisoners from Red Cross; memorandum provides clearest indication to date that military officials were troubled by practice even before Taguba's report; Lt Gen James R Helmly, leader of Army Reserve, suspends Brig Gen Janis L Karpinski, commander of military police brigade at Abu Ghraib, pending review of misconduct there while she was commander of prison; photo (M)
news.title: C.I.A. Bid to Keep Some Detainees Off Abu Ghraib Roll Worries Officials

news.abstract: Russian scientist at former Soviet biological weapons laboratory in Siberia dies after accidentally sticking herself with needle laced with deadly ebola virus, for which there is no vaccine or treatment; scientists and officials say accident raises concerns about safety and secrecy at State Research Center of Virology and Biotechnology, leading recipient of aid in American program to help former Soviet scientists and labs convert to peaceful research; American experts say accident did not occur in lab now receiving US government or private money for research (M)
news.title: Russian Scientist Dies in Ebola Accident at Former Weapons Lab

news.abstract: Israeli television stations are reporting that Atty Gen Menachem Mazuz has decided against indicting Prime Min Ariel Sharon on charges of accepting bribes from real estate developer; threat of indictment has been political handicap for Sharon as he tries to cajole and press ministers in his coalition government to support his plan to 'disengage' from Palestinians without peace agreement; Mazuz, whose spokesman refuses to confirm TV reports, is expected to make formal announcement of his decision on June 15 (M)
news.title: Sharon Reportedly Will Avoid Bribery Charges

news.title: IRAQ UPDATE

news.abstract: Congress Party yields to demands of one of its coalition partners for more cabinet positions, staving off short-term threat to cohesion of Indian Prime Min Manmohan Singh's new government but raising questions about its long-term stability; gives most of key posts to longtime party stalwarts known for loyalty to family of party leader Sonia Gandhi; must cater to demands of coalition partners who share little more than dislike for recently defeated Hindu nationalist party and love for power (M)
news.title: India's Coalition Survives Battle Over Cabinet

news.abstract: Shrine of Imam Ali, one of Shiite Muslims' holiest sites, suffers minor damage for second time in May as clashes continue between American forces and insurgents loyal to rebel cleric Moktada al-Sadr in Najaf and neighboring Kufa; American soldiers have taken great pains to avoid damaging shrine for fear of alienating Shiites; Gen Mark Kimmitt says it is unclear whether damage was caused by fighting between rival Shiite factions or intentionally by Sadr's men to blame Americans; Sadr's force blame American fire; Americans say Sadr's men may have tried to reoccupy mosque in downtown Karbala, but apparently ran off as American armored vehicles approached; bomb blast near Baghdad hotel wounds two people; second blast wounds American soldier; photos; diagram (M)
news.title: Shrine in Najaf Damaged Again as Clashes Continue

news.abstract: One policeman was killed and at least 26 people were injured today when two car bombs went off within an interval of 25 minutes in the southern port city of Karachi.

news.abstract: Pres Bush and Sen John Kerry differ little on broad outlines of their approaches to Iraq, although Kerry holds Bush has lost international credibility and that only new president can rally other nations to provide needed help; Bush's gradual shift toward policies advocated by Kerry makes it hard for Kerry to exploit what Democrats and Republicans view as Bush's biggest political crisis by stressing differences between them; chart compares their positions (M)
news.title: Candidates' Iraq Policies Share Many Similarities

news.abstract: Dr Hussain al-Shahristani, Iraqi nuclear scientist who spent several years in Abu Ghraib prison after breaking with Saddam Hussein over plans to develop atomic bomb, withdraws his name from consideration as interim leader of Iraq, saying he prefers to serve his country in other ways; he escaped to West in 1991; separately, American military announces capture in Najaf of Riyadh al-Nouri, Moktada al-Sadr's brother-in-law and crucial figure in Sadr's organization in Najaf; Nouri is handed over to Iraqi authorities for prosecution in connection with Apr 2003 murder of rival of Sadr; fierce fighting breaks out in Najaf between Sadr's militias and American troops; photo (M)
news.title: Top Candidate to Lead Iraq's Interim Government Says He Doesn't Want the Job

news.title: Names of the Dead

news.abstract: Shrine of Imam Hussein survives month of urban fighting in Karbala, but American reputation is marred; Iraqis seem to be angry not at insurgent army that took shelter in city, but at American army; they point to devastation wrought by three weeks of fighting, evident in wrecked hotels and bullet-riddled cars and ruined elementary school; before American army arrrived in Karbala, many of locals, especially businessmen, had grown tired of Mahdi Army, as had some of country's most powerful political and clerical leaders; they sent series of signals that many interpreted as green light for Americans to move into Karbala and Najaf with explicit condition that they stay out of two holy shrines and avoid damaging them; in fact, religious shrines received only minor damage, testament to what appears to be remarkable marksmanship by Americans; photos; maps (M)
news.title: Two Shrines Intact, but U.S Reputation Is Marred After Clashes With Rebels

news.abstract: Indonesian International Crisis Group leader Sidney Jones' work permit has expired and Indonesian government will not renew it; group has issued reports criticizing government (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Indonesia: Terror Expert Facing Expulsion

news.abstract: Planned renovation of Panama Canal so it could accommodate longer vessels might devastate poverty-stricken villages nearby; thousands of residents, most of them Indian, would be forced off their land; Indian activists and church groups have campaigned for months in villages to inform peasant farmers about proposed expansion of canal and educate them about their rights; photos; map (M)
news.title: Panama Journal; Panama Canal Thinks Big, Bringing Fear to the Jungle

news.abstract: Prime Minister Ariel Sharon of Israel has decided to present ministers with his original plan for a complete withdrawal.
news.title: Sharon, in Reversal, Proposes Full Pullout From Gaza Strip

news.abstract: Even college-educated applicants cannot find jobs in China, where leaders are struggling to control country's overheating economy; country's economy must roar just to keep unemployment from rising; putting brakes on growth, even gently, will increase unemployment rate; political pressure on Communist Party to continue creating jobs is enormous; more than 110 million migrant workers have left countryside for cities in search of jobs in factories or on construction sites; transition from planned economy to market economy cost tens of millions of workers their jobs with closings of inefficient state-owned enterprises; photos (M)
news.title: It's Out of College and Onto Jobless Rolls in China

news.abstract: Battles break out in Kufa, Iraq, killing at least five militiamen, day after declaration of truce between American soldiers and forces loyal to rebel Shiite cleric Moktada al-Sadr; each side accuses other of shooting first; both say they will honor truce; large bands of militiamen armed with AK-47's and heavy weapons roam streets of Kufa and neighboring Najaf; al-Sadr does not appaear at his Kufa mosque to deliver weekly sermon; his aide speaks instead, denouncing Americans; photo (M)

news.title: World Briefing | Asia: India: Party Admits Slogans Hurt

news.abstract: Ethiopia's effort to break cycle of starvation by relocating 2.2 million struggling farmers from highlands to more fertile Oromia lowlands has been disaster; program is well-intentioned, but poorly planned; government hoped to fix problems caused by farmers' unorganized migrations in search of more fertile land; Oromia settlers complain of malaria, hunger and water shortages; many are abandoning new homes to return to old homes, worse off than before; United Nations and donor governments were skeptical from start but are now being asked to help support settlers; photo, map (M)
news.title: Ethiopia's Bold Plan to Improve Life Makes It Worse

news.abstract: American troops clash with Mahdi Army of Moktada al-Sadr in Kufa for second day since cease-fire was declared; al-Sadr's spokesman blames US for provoking trouble and sending in Iraqi police from outside, but military says Mahdi Army fired rocket-propelled grenades at patrol, which returned fire and killed attackers; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Troops and Rebel Militia Clash Again

news.abstract: Most of the dozens of foreigners who had been trapped by four armed militants were freed, but details of the rescue and the mopping up operation remained murky.
news.title: Saudi Commandos Free Hostages, Ending Standoff With Militants

news.title: Clashes in Najaf and Kufa Put the Cease-Fire in Peril

news.abstract: Twenty death certificates for Afghan and Iraqi prisoners who died in US custody were completed by US military medical examiners in ten-day rush in May, even though some of deaths occurred months earlier; many of known investigations into abuses moved glacially until publication of notorious photos of abuse at Abu Ghraib prison; some of cases detailed; photo; chart (M)
news.title: Military Completed Death Certificates For 20 Prisoners Only After Months Passed

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon's plan to withdraw Jewish settlers from Gaza has support of most Israelis and Pres Bush, but seven-hour cabinet meeting ends with Sharon still apparently one vote short of winning over his own ministers; infighting reopens rivalry with Benjamin Netanyahu, finance minister and former prime minister; photo (M)
news.title: Sharon Still One Vote Short in Cabinet Debate on Gaza Plan

news.abstract: Boisterous oil town of Calgary is in fever pitch over Calgary Flames, team of also-rans that has emerged from years of lackluster skating and near financial ruin to become first Canadian club to make Stanley Club finals in decade; photos; map (M)
news.title: Calgary Journal; In a Nation of Hockey Fans, A City Reaches Fever Pitch

news.abstract: Saudi commandos in helicopters storm residential complex in Khobar, freeing most of dozens of foreign hostages trapped by four armed militants for 24 hours; photo; map; government reports 22 people killed by militants and 25 wounded, with militants' leader wounded and captured; three other gunmen use hostages as cover to escape in stolen car; attack on luxurious Oasis Residential Resorts is second brazen assault this month against Saudi oil industry and comes as country tries to increase production to ease record global oil prices; one American known dead; most of others are Indian or Filipino; seven American government workers reportedly eluded capture; assault details are murky; Saudi Amb Prince Bandar bin Sultan says oil production will not be disrupted by terrorists; Al Qaeda group claims responsibility (M)
news.title: SAUDI MILITARY STORMS COMPLEX TO FREE HOSTAGES

news.abstract: Gunmen kill leading pro-Taliban Sunni cleric, Mufti Nizammudin Shamzai, in Karachi, prompting enraged protesters to take to streets; Shamzai, soft-spoken religious scholar in his late 70's, had worked to bring together Pakistan's warring Islamic sects and was ardent supporter of Afghanistan's Taliban; many Taliban commanders attended his schools; photo (M)
news.title: Gunmen Kill a Leading Pro-Taliban Sunni Cleric in Pakistan

news.abstract: Pres Megawati Sukarnoputri, in rare news conference, makes no apologies for her government's decision to expel Sidney Jones, leading American expert on Indonesia's terrorist groups; Jones has written series of reports on inner workings of militant Islamic group Jemaah Islamiyah that have been praised by law enforcement and intelligence officials in Washington; director of Indonesia's intelligence agency, ally of Megawati, publicly complained about Jones's reports, as did cabinet members; Megawati suggests that Indonesia's willingness to fight against terrorists, and matter of Jones, are separate; says technically she has not expelled Jones, only refused to renew her work permit (M)

news.abstract: Nine older women and two men who live inside shattered building in Grozny, Chechnya, have survived through war and cold and hunger and illness, pulling one another along if any lagged behind; little group of mismatched neighbors is living off rubble that has collapsed around them, cleaning and selling bricks, one by one, to new breed of entrepreneur in Grozny, brick dealer; photo; map (M)
news.title: Grozny Journal; In a Ruined City, Even the Rubble Is Taken From Them

news.abstract: International Atomic Energy Agnency reports that Iran is still making parts and materials that could be used in manufacture of nuclear weapons, nearly two months after pledging to suspend nuclear program; Iranians insist they only want to produce commercial nuclear power, but agency report cites evidence that inspectors were misled, especially on where Iran obtained key components (M)
news.title: Iran Still Making Nuclear Materials, U.N. Agency Says

news.abstract: Fighters loyal to Moktada al-Sadr, Shiite radical who fashioned army from discontented of Iraq's slums, begin to withdraw from centers of Najaf and Kufa where they have been battling American forces since April; there are reports that Sadr has met with with Grand Ayatolla Ali al-Sistani, Iraq's most revered Shiite cleric; withdrawal, coupled with reported meeting of rival clerics, gives rise to hope that Sadr's rebellion might be ending; hundreds of Iraqis, including scores of civilians, have been killed since rebellion began and shrines have been damaged; Prime Min Iyad Allawi declares fighting is over, interview, and says Iraq will take control of thousands of Iraqi detainees held in American-controlled prisons; photo (M)

news.abstract: Prime Min Ariel Sharon coaxes Israel toward evacuation of some settlements next year, winning approval from right-wing coalition government to begin preparing for what he calls 'disengagement' from Palestinians of West Bank and Gaza; government decision falls short of original evacuation plan, but through mix of compromise and cajoling, including abrupt dismissal of two far-right ministers before vote, Sharon appears to be advancing toward goal despite fervent right-wing opposition; advisers say vote will permit him to pursue plan while preserving coalition and forestalling parliamentary elections, buying him months to build more support; plan has opened fissures within Likud party as well as provoking outrage from many right-wingers; Palestinian Prime Min Ahmed Qurei says Palestinians welcome Israeli withdrawal if it is total and comprehensive and Bush administration calls plan 'courageous'; Sharon's actions come without seeking peace agreement; asserts Palestinian leadership is not credible negotiating partner but says Israel must act now to avoid ceding more land in eventual internationally imposed solution; Israeli court sentences Marwan Barghouti to five consecutive life terms, plus 40 years, for his involvement in attacks that killed four Israelis and Greek monk; on entering court, Barghouti calls for Palestinian uprising to continue; map; photos (M)

news.title: New Wave of Repression Seen in Zimbabwe By-Election

news.abstract: Bush administration gives South Korea detailed plan for withdrawing one-third of 37,000 US troops on Korean peninsula by end of 2005, as part of wider effort to reposition US forces around globe; removal of 12,500 troops would be first reduction since 1992 and would include previously announced transfer of brigade of about 3,600 soldiers to Iraq this summer; South Korean conservatives accuse Pres Roh Moo Hyun of allowing anti-American views to flourish, provoking US; photo; conservatives also say shift would surrender bargaining chip useful in nuclear arms talks with North Korea; Sec Donald Rumsfeld is reassessing strategies and new technologies worldwide
news.title: U.S. May Cut Third of Troops In South Korea

news.abstract: Whenever I think of D-Day, it is not some Normandy beach that springs to mind but a peaceful French village about 15 kilometers inland. It is a pretty place called Fontaine-Henry, its houses built of a warm golden stone, and on one side of the village green a memorial to the dead of World War I. On the other there is a picture-postcard château, and next to it, the church. Walk through the gate and up the steps, turning left at the top. Underneath the yew tree, if you look closely, you will see that the churchyard wall is pitted with scars.
news.title: D-Day / 60 YEARS LATER: Sacrifices in Normandy live on in the European memory

news.abstract: Bush administration insists that plans to withdraw one-third of 37,000 American troops will not be seen by North Korea as weakening of commitment to South Korea or as lessening of resolve to dismantle North Korean nuclear arsenal; photo; Deputy Under Sec Richard Lawless explains position (M)
news.title: U.S. Defends Plan to Reduce Forces in South Korea

news.abstract: SAINTE-MERE-EGLISE, France—  Sixty years is a long time, especially when measured in the seasonal rhythms of the Normandy countryside, of horses foaling and apples to be picked and pressed into cider. But for the elderly residents of this ancient village, at least for the handful of hardy survivors old enough to remember, the events of D-Day are so vivid they seem to have happened only a decade or so ago.
news.title: D-Day / 60 YEARS LATER: Out of the night sky like phantoms:Sainte-Mère-Eglise remembers

news.abstract: Hearing in Moscow court moves Mikhail Khodorovsky closer to trial, eight months after oligarch was arrested at gunpoint on Siberian airfield, charged with defrauding government and evading taxes; family and friends appear in court to show support; photo (M)
news.title: Friends and Relatives Rally as a Top Russian's Bribery Trial Inches Forward

news.abstract: RHYNERN, Germany—  There are miniature flags. Grainy photographs from the 1940s. Endless rows of titles on Normandy and war on the bookshelves. There are letters, certificates, pamphlets, maps and more photos. A painting of an armed speedboat and embroidery work from the Norman town of Bayeux adorn the walls.
news.title: D-DAY / 60 years later : For past enemies, unity in horrors remembered in common

news.abstract: Senior intelligence officials say Central Intelligence Agency has yet to put in place plan to address operational flaw rooted in practices that severely limit how much data about human sources is shared with analysts who produce intelligence assessments; Dir George J Tenet gave subordinates 30 days to devise solution in Feb after finding that problem contributed to errors in CIA's prewar estimates on Iraq; team headed by A B Krongard has only recently carried out pilot program that has not yet been broadly adopted; difficulty of devising solution reflects deep gulf between CIA's operations directorate, which recruits and supervises spies, and intelligence directorate, which draws broad conclusions from raw data from all sources (M)
news.title: Despite a Pledge to Speed Work, Fixing an Internal Problem Takes Time at the C.I.A.

news.title: With Potential for a Harsh Summer, Basic City Services Become the Priority

news.abstract: Terrorism task force of Council on Foreign Relations is scheduled to present report to Senate committee that commends Saudi Arabia for recent efforts to curtail terrorist financing, but asserts that opportunities for financing of terrorism persist; all members of task force endorsed report, which praised Bush administration's antiterrorism efforts but said they had not gone far enough; early draft of report became so mired in internal conflict over its tone that some members feared i t would never be published; report's authors are William F Wechsler and Lee S Wolosky, former members of Clinton administration; task force chmn is Maurice R Greenberg and vice chmn is Mallory Factor; they are major fund-raisers for Pres Bush (M)

news.abstract: Bush administration is considering toughening its policy toward Sudan over events in Darfur, where thousands of people have been killed and over million driven from their homes by Arab militias that many in region say are linked to Sudanese Army; Bush officials are considering whether what is happening in Darfur amounts to genocide; Sec of State Colin L Powell says link between militias and government is strong, and that many people are still at risk of dying in Darfur and across bor der in Chad; map; photo (M)
news.title: White House Reconsiders Its Policy on Crisis in Sudan

news.abstract: Russia liberalizes penalties for possession of small amounts of illegal drugs; makes possession of small amounts for personal use punishable by fine, though possession of larger amounts or trafficking is punishable by prison term; laws were already similar to those in West in theory, but actual sentences have been harsh even for possession of small amounts of drugs; special commission has redefined table of weights and penalties, bringing them closer to those accepted by world community (M)

news.abstract: Irish voters appear to have overwhelming voted to eliminate constitutional provision granting automatic citizenship to babies born in Ireland; Ireland is only European Union member state with such a rule; vote marks victory for government, which argued pregnant women come to Ireland so children will be entitled to European Union residence and welfare benefits; children born in Ireland of non-Irish parents will still have right to citizenship if at least one parent has lived there for three of previous four years (M)

news.abstract: Senior military and intelligence officials say United States launched 50 failed airstrikes, far more than previously disclosed, and targeted broader array of Iraqi leaders during early days of war last year than has previously been admitted; say some strikes caused significant civilian casualties; say raids targeted 13 Iraqi leaders and were seemingly undercut by poor intelligence; targets included Gen Izzat Ibrahim and Maj Gen Rafi Abd al-Latif Tilfah, who now play leadership role in anti-American insurgency; photos (M)

news.abstract: Success of AIDS clinic in Serowe, Botswana, hospital, is portend for nation, where nearly 4 in 10 adults are HIV positive, and most of rest of sub-Saharan Africa; Botswana, with world's highest HIV infection rate, has declared AIDS national emergency and hopes to eventually supply antiretroviral drugs to all who need them; began to turn tide since Jan, when Pres Festus Mogae ordered routine AIDS tests of everyone who comes into hospital or clinic; doctors say they are now catching people before they are seriously ill; map; graph; photos (M)
news.title: Mandatory Tests Bolster Botswana's War on AIDS

news.abstract: The Philippine Congress concluded the counting of votes in the presidential election, with results showing the incumbent, Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo, winning.

news.abstract: Beheading of Paul M Johnson Jr by Islamic militants in Saudi Arabia brings out displays of sympathy and grieving in his hometown of Little Egg Harbor, NJ, but one sign speaks of growing anger against Muslims; several townspeople say they share sentiment; Muslim officials around state and around world have been quick to condemn killing and offer sympathy to Johnson's family (M)
news.title: After Beheading, Rising Anger in New Jersey

news.abstract: Andrea Volpe, who was arrested on charges of shooting his girlfriend and burying her alive, leads Italian police to grave of two missing teenagers in woods at Busto Arsizio, northwest of Milan; Volpe and dead teenagers were members of heavy metal band Beasts of Satan; Volpe told police band members were killed in Satanic rite on Jan 17, 1998; police have arrested three other band members; police have widened investigation to look at other unsolved disappearances and killings in region; devil worship is growing problem among Italian young people; photo; map (M)
news.title: Italian Police Look to a Cult In '98 Killings Of Teenagers

news.abstract: Philippine Congress concludes that Pres Gloria Macapagal Arroyo has won re-election by more than million votes; counting votes from May 11 election took weeks that were marked by acrimonious debates; supporters of closest rival Fernando Poe Jr accuse administration of election fraud and threaten to contest results before Supreme Court (M)
news.title: Arroyo Said to Win Bitter Philippines Race

news.abstract: Algerian Army kills Nabil Sahraoui, leader of Salafist Group for Preaching and Combat, North Africa's largest and most dangerous Islamic terrorist organization; gun battle culminates intense government drive against Al Qaeda's affiliates in region; Sahraoui's death follows reports that group's founder Hassan Hattab is dead; Algerian military officer is quoted as saying group's leadership has been 'completely neutralized'; Sahraoui, also known as Abu Ibrahim Mustafa, was killed with four other senior members of group; photo (M)
news.title: Militant Slain In Algeria; Ties to Qaeda Are Reported

news.abstract: Saudi security forces comb Riyadh, looking for body of murdered American hostage Paul M Johnson Jr; concern grows that knowledge of his whereabouts died with killing of his captors; group that claimed responsibility for kidnapping, an Al Qaeda offshoot, vows to continue struggle despite death of its leader (M)
news.title: Saudis Seek American's Body as Militants Vow More Terror

news.abstract: As South Korean television broadcast pleas from a Korean hostage, officials said they would go ahead with plans to send 3,000 troops to Iraq.
news.title: Seoul to Send Troops to Iraq Despite Kidnapping

news.abstract: Iraq's newly appointed government considers imposing state of emergency that could involve curfews and ban on public demonstrations to counter violent resistance it faces even before it assumes power; Prime Min Iyad Allawi, who worked closely with Central Intelligence Agency in opposing Saddam Hussein's govenment in 1990's, says in his first news briefing that he will consider 'human rights principles and international law,' but that he intends to act quickly and forcefully against insurgency, using extraordinary methods if necessary; such measures could be applied in Falluja, where United States forces have been battling guerrilla fighters for several weeks, and Sadr City, Baghdad slum where three Iraqis were killed on June 20 in confrontations with American soldiers; other measures being considered by new Iraqi government include ban on public demonstrations, checkpoints and changes to search and seizure laws; photos (M)
news.title: IRAQ GOVERNMENT CONSIDERS USING EMERGENCY RULE

news.abstract: Heavy fighting erupts in Russian republic of Ingushetia, region bordering Chechnya, as insurgents stage coordinated attacks on police and other security buildings in at leat three cities; official Russian Information Agency reports at least 13 people killed; others put death toll at 46, not including insurgents who may have died; fighting comes after Aslan Maskhadov, former elected president of Chechnya, now a prominent rebel field commander, said he decided to shift from guerrilla tactics to offensive operations directly against Russia's federal forces and pro-Moscow Chechen allies in region; map (M)
news.title: Heavy Fighting Erupts in Russian Region Bordering Chechnya

news.abstract: Bangladesh government charges Proshika, aid organization, founder Qazi Faruque Ahmed and six others in organization with sedition; Ahmed is already in jail on corruption charges and claims anti-Islamic fundamentalist government is harassing him with false charges (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: Bangladesh: New Charges For Aid Group's Founder

news.abstract: Iran seizes three small British Royal Navy boats and arrests all eight sailors on board, saying boats entered Iranian waters without permission; sailors were stopped at Shatt al Arab, stretch of water marking southern boundary between Iran and Iraq; navy was delivering boats to Iraqi Riverine Patrol Service; British officials seek to play down boat incident as relatively minor; arrests come during time of strained relations between Iran and Britain, mostly over war in Iraq and Iran's nuclear capacity; map (M)
news.title: Iran Seizes 3 British Navy Boats and Detains 8 Sailors in a Territorial Dispute on Iraqi Border

news.abstract: White House is said to be debating whether to act this summer to select permanent successor to George J Tenet, director of central intelligence who is stepping down on July 11; Pres Bush is reconsidering earlier plan to leave John McLaughlin in place as acting director through Nov election rather than risk confirmation battle in Senate this summer; people involved in discussion say there is concern that failure to select permanent successor may be both practical and political mistake; those being considered for post include Rep Porter J Goss, Rep Christopher Cox and Robert M Gates, director of central intelligence in first Bush administration; photos (M)
news.title: Bush Considers Replacing C.I.A. Chief More Quickly

news.abstract: UNITED NATIONS.
news.title: World Briefings

news.abstract: FBI Dir Robert S Mueller III predicts bureau will someday be part of 'official international terrorism alliance' akin to NATO, speech to Council on Foreign Relations; reports preliminary talks among NATO members on forging more formal intelligence ties (S)
news.title: F.B.I. Chief Sees NATO-like Antiterror Alliance

news.abstract: Audacious overnight raid by heavily armed militants in southern Russian republic neighboring Chechnya kills at least 75 people and wounds dozens more; photos; fighters withdraw with minimal losses and cache of captured weapons; raid aimed at police and security posts in Nazran, Ingushetia, is largest by Chechen separatists since 1999; Pres Vladimir Putin flies to region (M)
news.title: 75 Die as Chechen Rebels Stage Raid Across Border

news.abstract: State Department, in revised report, says number of significant international terrorism episodes rose slightly in 2003, and that number of those injured went up by more than fifty percent, contradicting Bush administration's earlier claims; reports 208 episodes and 3,646 injuries; Sec Colin Powell discusses report; chart (M)
news.title: State Department Report Shows Increase in Terrorism

news.abstract: WHO and Unicef warn that polio is surging in Nigeria and spreading to other countries, putting West and Central Africa on brink of largest epidemic in recent years; map showing number of cases since last year; 60 cases were reported by Nigeria in last week of April and Sudan is now tenth country with strain that originated in Nigeria; health organizations and Rotary International say goal of eradication by end of decade can still be met if funding is provided to immunize 74 million children in 22 African countries in synchronized program this fall (M)
news.title: Spread of Polio in Africa Makes U.N. Fear a Major Epidemic

news.abstract: Iraq update; map
news.title: IRAQ UPDATE

news.abstract: United States, bowing to broad opposition on United Nations Security Council, drops its effort to gain immunity for its troops from prosecution by International Criminal Court; outcome is political defeat for Washington; American diplomats, confident of obtaining routine 'technical rollover' of measure as they have in last two years, appear to have miscalculated impact of publicity given American mistreatment of Iraqi detainees; they were also caught off guard by Secretary Gen Kofi Annan's strong opposition; it will have no effect on vulnerability to prosecution of American soldiers in Iraq because neither US nor Iraq is member of tribunal, and its jurisdiction is limited to countries that do not themselves prosecute crimes by their military; Annan says decision by US not to pursue immunity resolution will help maintain unity of Security Council (M)
news.title: U.S. DROPS PLAN TO EXEMPT G.I.'S FROM U.N. COURT

news.abstract: Gen Omar Suleiman, director of Egyptian intelligence, visits top Israeli and Palestinian officials to work out precise role Egypt would play in overseeing security in Gaza Strip once Israel relinquishes coastal territory to Palestinians; Israel insists on managing security at Gaza's airport and seaport, while Egypt would prefer international forces there; Egypt wants to exercise some supervision over training of Palestinian security forces, and wants ministerial responsibility for security to be transferred from Palestinian Authority's chairman Yasir Arafat to Palestinian prime minister's office; Arafat has resisted both ideas so far (M)
news.title: Egyptian Aide in Talks on Future Security Role in Gaza

news.abstract: Colombian Internal Affairs office report, obtained by New York Times, shows that soldiers who said they accidentally killed family of five peasants from long distance mistaking them for guerillas shot at least one from less than two feet away; Colombian President Alvaro Uribe has issued public apology for events that killed baby and three teenagers (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Colombia: Army Report Undercut

news.abstract: ASIA; MIDDLE EAST; EUROPE; AFRICA; AMERICAS
news.title: World Briefing

news.abstract: There were some signs, meanwhile, that President Bush's continued quest for an explicit NATO role in Iraq might meet with success.
news.title: Turkey Blast Won't Disrupt Bush's Visit

news.abstract: Swiss Foreign Ministry reports that France has agreed to pay 3 million euros for damages caused by protesters at Group 8 summit at Evian (France) on border with Switzerland; payment is on top of 12 million euro payment France agreed to prior to summit to cover Swiss security concerns (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Switzerland: Compensation From France

news.abstract: New China News Agency reports that Chinese Maritime Search and Rescue Center and China Ocean Shipping Company conducted joint operation simulating suicide bomb attack on tanker in South China Sea (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Asia: China: Guarding Against Suicide Boats

news.abstract: Defense Dept confirms deaths of three service members in Iraq, bringing total to 847 since start of war (S)
news.title: Names of the Dead

news.abstract: American officials in Iraq obtain document showing that Iraqi intelligence agents had contacts with Osama bin Laden when he was in Sudan in mid-1990's as part of broad effort by Baghdad to work with organizations opposing Saudi ruling family; document states that Iraq agreed to rebroadcast anti-Saudi propaganda, but that request from bin Laden to begin joint operations against foreign forces in Saudi Arabia went unanswered; there is no further indication of collaboration; document is internal report by Iraqi intelligence service on its efforts to seek cooperation with several Saudi opposition groups, including bin Laden's organization before Al Qaeda had become full-fledged terrorist organization; Bush administration has said there was considerable evidence of ties between Iraq and Al Qaeda, but independent 9/11 commission concluded that contacts did not demonstrate 'collaborative relationship' between Iraq and Al Qaeda (M)
news.title: Iraqis, Seeking Foes of Saudis, Contacted bin Laden, File Says

news.abstract: Iran frees eight British servicemen who spent three nights in Iranian custody after their boats strayed into Iranian waters; British diplomats meet with eight in southern Iran and fly with them to British Embassy in Tehran; photo (M)
news.title: Iran Frees British Servicemen Seized in Boats

news.abstract: Iraq update; map (S)
news.title: IRAQ UPDATE

news.abstract: Nikolai M Girenko, Russian ethnologist who fought racist groups, was shot and killed by two young men in his St Petersburg apartment on June 19; wrote booklet to guide prosecutors and police officers investigating explosion of ethnically motivated crimes by skinheads, neo-Nazis and other hate groups; officials concede that he may have been killed for his work against these groups; photo (M)
news.title: A Russian Fighting Hate Is Killed in Hate

news.abstract: Women in Afghanistan are registering to vote for first time, but strict rules of tribal culture are hampering process; women in conservative Muslim districts of southern provinces rarely leave their homes, and female registration teams must visit every household individually; whether women will vote in fall's parliamentary and presidential elections may depend on whether their husbands let them out of house; photos (M)
news.title: Out of Sight, Afghans Register Women to Vote

news.abstract: Defense Dept confirms death of US soldier in Iraq
news.title: Names of the Dead

news.abstract: First Armored Division was given its final mission in Iraq in April: wrest control of string of southern towns from rebellious Shiite cleric Moktada al-Sadr's militia; division's operation is being studied by Army struggling to learn lessons of war that continues to evolve, even on eve of transfer of power; campaign was mix of military tactics, political maneuverings, media management and generous dollop of cash for rebuilding war-ravaged cities; formula could become model for future fighting against insurrections plaguing Iraq; Sadr remains at large, and question is whether tactical successes claimed by commanders have guaranteed lasting strategic victory; photos (M)
news.title: Army Used Speed and Might, Plus Cash, Against Shiite Rebel

news.abstract: Israeli troops in Nablus kill Nayef Abu Sharkh of Al Aksa Martyrs Brigades, Sheikh Ibrahim, West Bank leader of Islamic Jihad, and five others, including one member of Hamas; men were found in hidden room and died in gunfight (M)
news.title: 7 Militants Die In Israeli Raid In West Bank

news.abstract: Taliban claims responsibility for bomb which destroys bus carrying election workers near Jalalabad, killing two women and wounding three people seriously, including one child; driver may have detonated bomb after parking outside military base; women were voter registration officials (M)
news.title: Blast Kills 2 Afghan Women On Election Workers' Bus

news.abstract: A militant Iraqi group said it would behead an American marine unless the U.S. released all Iraqi prisoners.
news.title: Iraq Group Issues Threat to Behead a Missing Marine

news.abstract: China gives Internet democracy advocate Du Daobin suspended sentence; some applaud show of leniency, but others warn that magnanimity conceals push for tighter controls; estimated 30,000 Internet police monitor users, blocking sites and killing discussion threads on bulletin boards; provincial governments are adding their own controls; Internet bar users in Shanghai must now swipe cards with their national identity number to track use; analysts believe China is deeply concerned about blogging as medium of expression; photo (M)
news.title: Despite an Act of Leniency, China Has Its Eye on the Web

news.abstract: Pres Bush, in Ireland for annual United States-European Union summit, says 'bitter differences' between United States and Europe over war in Iraq are in past, but antiwar protests delay news conference; Bush hopes NATO will agree at summit in Istanbul to help train Iraqi security forces; 10,000 protesters march in Dublin prior to meeting; 6,000 soldiers and police dug trenches and threw up earth embankments around meeting site to discourage protesters; photo (M)
news.title: Amid Protests, Bush Sees Thaw in Europe Over Iraq

news.abstract: The official transfer was moved up by two days in an apparent bid to surprise insurgents who may have tried to sabotage the step toward self rule.
news.title: Handover Completed Early to Thwart Attacks, Officials Say

news.abstract: But the two sides did announce more measures to build confidence between the nuclear-armed neighbors.
news.title: India and Pakistan Report Little Progress as Talks Resume

news.abstract: By shifting power two days early, officials hoped to foil attacks by insurgents whom U.S. forces are still struggling to vanquish.
news.title: Extent of Government's Control Unclear as It Formally Steps In

news.abstract: President Bush said today that coalition forces in Iraq would support a possible decision by the new Iraqi leadership to declare martial law to deal with escalating violence and terror attacks.
news.title: U.S.-Led Forces Would Back Martial Law, Bush Says

news.abstract: Chechen refugees in republic of Ingushetia say they are being blamed for success of Islamic guerrillas who overran police station and checkpoints last week, systematically executing law enforcement and military personnel who tried to stop them; Russian and Ingush police are accusing Chechen refugees of assisting and sheltering guerrillas; thousands of Chechens are fleeing Ingushetia for Grozny, heeding implicit message that to stay is to risk their lives; photo; map (M)
news.title: Guerrilla Raids Force Chechen Refugees to Flee Again

news.abstract: Scene inside hospital in Baghdad is portrait of weariness on day Americans cede formal sovereignty to Iraqis; neither doctors nor patients have great expectations for new government; many patients are civilians, adults and children hit by stray bullets and rockets on streets of Baghdad; photo (M)
news.title: At a Baghdad Hospital, Fear and Resignation Remain on an Unexpectedly Ordinary Day

news.abstract: United States and Philippines will hold joint military exercises in Philippines in counterterrorism training program aimed at destroying local cells of Jemaah Islamiyah, Southeast Asian network with links to Al Qaeda (S)
news.title: U.S. to Aid Antiterror Plan in Philippines

news.abstract: Supreme Court rejects police interrogation tactic designed to induce suspects to give incriminating statements after purposely delaying Miranda warnings; tactic has been growing in popularity and is taught in police training courses; court's 5-to-4 decision against strategy invalidates murder case in Missouri (M)
news.title: Tactic of Delayed Miranda Warning Is Barred

news.abstract: Israeli tanks rolled into the northeastern corner of the Gaza Strip today with the aim of silencing Palestinian rocket fire.
news.title: Israelis Roll Into Gaza to Find Rocket Sites

news.abstract: Text of L Paul Bremer III's farewell letter to members of Iraq's Coalition Provisional Authority (M)
news.title: Parting Words From Bremer, Acceptance From Allawi and Congratulations From Bush

news.abstract: Gen Lino Oviedo, former military commander and presidential contender, returns to Paraguay after over five years in exile to contest criminal charges against him; was sentenced to 10 years in prison for leading 1996 coup attempt and faces trial on other charges (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Americas: Paraguay: Former Strongman Returns

news.abstract: Pres Bush calls on Muslim nations to embrace democracy, warning Mideast autocrats, including American allies, must recognize 'direction of events of the day,' speech at end of NATO summit meeting, Istanbul; again stresses need to confront terrorism by forcefully encouraging Muslim nations to modernize; themes of democracy and terrorism infused much of discussion at meeting; Turkish officials say package containing plastic explosive exploded on Turkish Airlines plane parked at Istanbul airport, injuring two workers; NATO leaders agree to send up to 3,500 more troops to Afghanistan, but reject Pres Hamid Karzai's plea to send soldiers now; photo (M)
news.title: Bush Urges All Autocrats To Yield Now To Democracy

news.abstract: International Atomic Energy Agency head Mohamed ElBaradei says Russia's project to help Iran build civilian nuclear reactor is not cause for international concern, even though agency probes charges that Iran secretly develops nuclear arms, meeting with Russian Pres Vladimir V Putin, near Moscow; effectively endorses Russia's plans to insist that Iran return any spent nuclear fuel at plant (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia: Iran Project No Worry, Nuclear Chief Says

news.abstract: China is clamping down on travel by Chinese tourists to Hong Kong to prevent news of expected huge pro-democracy march in Hong Kong from spreading on mainland; march will protest China's decision not to allow general elections in Hong Kong; Hong Kong's leading democrats are split over how aggressively to challenge China (M)
news.title: China Tries to Block News of Hong Kong's Pro-Democracy March

news.abstract: European Court of Human Rights rejects appeal by Turkish student barred from attending Istanbul university wearing head scarf; holds ban is not discriminatory (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: European Court Backs Ban On Muslim Scarves

news.abstract: Sixty Bosnian Serb politicians and officials, including interior minister and speaker of Parliament, are dismissed for their failure to arrest region's leading war crimes suspect Dr Radovan Karadzic; Lord Ashdown, international high representative for Bosnia, also freezes bank accounts of main Bosnian Serb party and several major companies; list of those removed from office includes mayors, police commanders and members of Parliament; officials in Ashdown's office say cost of continuing to support Karadzic will be much higher now that funds have been frozen and jobs have been lost (M)
news.title: 60 Bosnian Serbs Dismissed For Aid to War Crimes Figure

news.abstract: Eight-year study by Harvard researchers finds that daily vitamin pill can delay progress of AIDS in HIV-infected women; researchers say vitamins are not a cure or substitute for antiretroviral therapy, but for malnourished women in Africa or Asia with little hope of getting better drugs, vitamins are cheap, safe way of giving them extra months of life and little less misery before they die; study is published in The New England Journal of Medicine; World Health Orgn says six million people in poor countries are already sick enough to need antiretroviral drugs, but only 400,000 are getting them; efforts to increase that number are hindered by high drug prices, fights over patents, lack of money from donors, reluctance by African leaders to admit their nations have epidemics and inability of shattered health care systems to muster enough doctors, nurses and laboratories to safely deliver drugs (M)
news.title: Daily Vitamin Can Thwart AIDS Progress, Study Says

news.abstract: Hundreds of thousands showed a new boldness in denouncing mainland China for banning general elections.
news.title: Thousands of Protesters in Hong Kong Take Aim at Beijing

news.abstract: About one in six soldiers returning from war in Iraq shows signs of post-traumatic stress disorder or other emotional difficulties; study published in New England Journal of Medicine is first to examine mental health of troops returning from Iraq; researchers surveyed more than 6,000 soldiers in months before and after service in Iraq and in Afghanistan, where lower levels of psychiatric problems are found among troops; 17 percent of those who fought in Iraq report major depression, severe anxiety or post-traumatic stress disorder, compared with 11 percent of troops who served in Afghanistan; rates are slightly higher than those found amnong soldiers in Persian Gulf war, but lower than rates in Vietnam veterans; however, mental health studies of soldiers in those earlier conflicts were carried out years after troops returned home; graph (M)
news.title: 1 in 6 Iraq Veterans Is Found to Have Stress-Related Disorder

news.abstract: Excerpt from Israeli Supreme Court decision on barrier being built between Israel and West Bank (M)
news.title: Israel's High Court: 'No Security Without Law'

news.abstract: Italian authorities begin enforcing new rules requiring people of ages 14 to 17 to secure so-called mini-driving license to take to roads on scooters, which are ubiquitous in country; authorities in most cities report that number of people taking test to get license is only small fraction of number supposed to take test; it is not clear how many illicit scooter-riders have been stopped by police officers empowered to impose fines and to confiscate offenders' motorcycles; photo (M)
news.title: . . . And Other Italian Engines Are Stilled by Bureaucracy

news.abstract: Governments across Middle East largely keep silent about extraordinary appearance of Arab leader--Saddam Hussein--in the dock; some in Arab countries outside Iraq are pleased to see dictator being arraigned, but many others say court appearance merely extends sense of Arab humiliation that grew out of American invasion; foreign ministers in Egypt and Jordan refuse to comment; sole official voice supporting trial comes from Kuwait, where American invasion of Iraq is seen as revenge for Hussein's invasion of Kuwait in 1990; photo (M)
news.title: A Sense of Arab Humiliation, but a Warning to Despotic Rulers

news.abstract: MILAN—  'Night and Day," crooned the music as Giorgio Armani ended the final collection of his 69th year by paying homage to his workers. They were lined up, all in white, behind a gauze backcloth as Armani, who turns 70 this month, bounded out to take his bow.
news.title: Armani stays 70 years young

news.abstract: WASHINGTON:—  Amid fears of open-ended military engagements in Iraq and Afghanistan, and ever more urgent-sounding indications of how stretched U.S. forces are around the globe, rumors that the military draft might be reinstated have surged across the United States, moving in recent months from obscure Internet sites into the mainstream media.
news.title: Is the draft coming back?American rumor mill thinks so

news.abstract: A botched rocket attack on two hotels used by foreigners paralyzed the city center.
news.title: New Swell of Insurgent Violence Rolls into Baghdad

news.abstract: China begins filtering billions of telephone text messages to ensure that people do not use communications tool to undermine one-party rule; campaign comes after text messages sent between China's nearly 300 million mobile phone users helped to expose national cover-up of SARS epidemic in 2003; photo (M)
news.title: China Is Filtering Phone Text Messages to Regulate Criticism

news.abstract: Police trainee Akbar Niazi on May 7 blew himself up inside Shiite Muslim mosque, killing 25 people in attack that marked beginning of six weeks of religious and political violence in Karachi, Pakistan; attacks have left 70 people dead, 200 wounded and Karachi destabilized; have also raised questions about effectiveness of Pres Pervez Musharraf's government, number of young Pakistanis joining militant groups and possible infiltration of Pakistan's army and police forces; photos (M)
news.title: As Terror Attacks Return, Reasons Haunt Pakistanis

news.abstract: Intelligence officials who fear terrorism at Athens Olympics say delays in completing security apparatus and athletic facilities have left too little time to fully test systems meant to detect or respond to attack; say security command center will not be operating completely until mid-July; say Science Applications International Corp, US-led consortium building system, has provided defective software and failed to complete work on command center by May 28 deadline; map; photos (M)
news.title: Delays in Athens Raise Concern On Olympic Security Readiness

news.abstract: Abu Hafs al-Masri Brigades, obscure group claiming ties to Al Qaeda, says terrorist attacks will begin in Europe after 'truce' offered by Osama bin Laden earlier in year expires in two weeks; terrorism experts say threat is hoax (M)
news.title: Group Tied to Al Qaeda Warns Europe of Attacks in Near Future

news.abstract: US military jailers at Abu Ghraib prison received important batch of prisoners within days after Saddam Hussein's capture in Dec 2003; they were bodyguards and other loyalists who tended to Hussein in his final weeks on run; military intelligence soldiers at prison say capture of bodyguards led to all-out push for information about Hussein's close supporters who were suspected of plotting against US occupation; say interrogators were given greater latitude to use tactics on new prisoners that had previously required signed approval of senior officers; say tactics included sleep and food deprivation, extended isolation and use of menacing dogs; worst known abuses at Abu Ghraib occurred before Hussein's capture, and involved members of military police who have said their actions were encouraged by prison officials (M)
news.title: Capture of Hussein Aides Spurred U.S. Interrogators

news.abstract: JAKARTA, Indonesia July 4 — As Indonesians prepare to vote on Monday in the first direct presidential elections since the fall of the Suharto regime, the biggest question is whether the front-runner, a former general, can muster the more than 50 percent of the vote he will need to avoid a runoff.
news.title: Indonesians Prepare to Vote on Monday

news.abstract: International Herald Tribune.
news.title: Iraqi Prime Minister Says al-Sadr Might Get Amnesty

news.abstract: Abdullah al-Hassan bin-Mahmoud, leader of Ansar al-Sunna militant group, posts message on Internet, claiming to have beheaded Marine Cpl Wassef Ali Hassoun; it is unclear whether this is true, or what relationship is between Ansar al-Sunna and 20th Revolution Regiment which earlier released video claiming to have kidnapped Hassoun; Ansar al-Sunna includes some of most violent elements from Ansar al-Islam militant group of northern Iraq; photo (M)
news.title: Militant Iraqi Group Says It Beheaded a Kidnapped American Marine

news.abstract: Gen Susilo Bambang Yudhoyono is front-runner going into first round of Indonesian presidential elections on July 5; polls give him 43.5 percent of vote, but not 50 percent needed to avoid run-off election; closest rival Gen Wiranto has only 14.2 percent of vote; incumbent Pres Megawati Sukarnoputri has little support; Yudhoyono's supporters hope that he will bring change and stability without pushing religious agenda; photos; map (M)
news.title: Indonesians Hope a Real Election on Monday Will Bring Real Change

news.abstract: American and British officials say United States returned five terrorism suspects to Saudi Arabia from Guantanamo Bay, Cuba, in May 2003 as part of three-way deal intended to satisfy important allies in invasion of Iraq; say Saudi officials later freed five Britons and two others convicted of terrorist attacks in Saudi Arabia as part of deal; British diplomats believe men were tortured by Saudis into false confessions; Pentagon, Central Intelligence Agency and Justice Department officials reportedly opposed transfer of Saudis initially, questioning whether some detainees were too dangerous and whether Saudis would keep promises to imprison them; releases were public relations coups for Saudi Arabia and Britain, which faced domestic criticism of their roles in Iraq war; National Security Council denies Saudis were transferred in return for Britons; Saudi officials give contradictory accounts of whereabouts of five and of their legal status; photos (M)
news.title: OFFICIALS DETAIL A DETAINEE DEAL BY 3 COUNTRIES

news.abstract: Former Gen. Bambang Susilo Yudhoyono was likely to win but will probably face a run-off in September.
news.title: Ex-General Leads Vote in Indonesia

news.abstract: State Department authorizes voluntary departure of its employees' families and nonemergency personnel at US Embassy in Bahrain after warning that terrorist attacks on Americans might be imminent; action follows order by Pentagon to pull out families of defense personnel and other employees at major base that supports US Navy's Fifth Fleet; warnings come two weeks after authorities in Bahrain arrest, then release, six men who were initially suspected of planning attacks; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Authorizes Families to Leave Bahrain

news.abstract: Russia's Communist Party convenes meeting, but internal strife and outmaneuvering by Pres Vladimir Putin leave party at its weakest point since its return in 1993 after two-year ban; slide toward irrelevance signifies ascendancy of Putin and what analysts describe as attendant risks of that rise; turnabout has been swift, with number of seats in 450-seat Duma dropping from 113 to 51 in last election; breakaway faction meets separately and claims to have rounded up quorum, but Zyuganov refuses to recognize revolt; political chaos mirrors underlying ideological confusion; photos (M)
news.title: Communists' Slide Weakens Checks on Putin's Power

news.abstract: Tables are turned in Iraq as some of those who were imprisoned and tortured during Saddam Hussein regime, or who fled country, now hold seats of power and air their charges against him in court; crowds around nation are transfixed by television replays of Hussein's exchanges with judge; photo (M)
news.title: Tables Turned, a Victim Sees Persecutor in Court

news.abstract: Recap of latest activities in Iraq; map (M)
news.title: IRAQ UPDATE

news.abstract: NEW YORK:—  When Simon Jeruchim was 12, the French police raided and sealed his family's apartment in Montreuil, on the outskirts of Paris.
news.title: For some, French settlement is $3,000 : For Nazi victims, a low payout rate from banks

news.abstract: Love story involving couple in Goryeong, South Korea, has happy ending after 58 years; man left woman in 1943 to pursue riches by working in Japanese-ruled Sakhalin Island, intending to stay two years; he and other Koreans were prevented from leaving when Soviets took over island; in 2001, he did come home and was reunited with his love; now she, age 80, is hospitalized and he, age 82, visits daily to tend to her; photo; map (M)
news.title: Goryeong Journal; A Young Love Defies Both Distance and the Decades

news.abstract: When 21-year-old Izumi Mori , in a wedding gown, closes her grandmother's show on Wednesday, it will be the end of a 50-year love affair with fashion for Hanae Mori.
news.title: Goodbye, butterfly

news.abstract: The Palestinian dead included four militants, but the ISraeli military also acknowledged the deaths of "two innocent Palestinians."
news.title: Six Palestinians and Israeli Killed in Clashes

news.abstract: Armada of American, British and Australian warships is circling Iraq's offshore oil depots to prevent threat of waterborne suicide attackers; Iraqi oil flows through rattling pipelines to depots; vulnerable site is crucial to country's economic future; in April, attackers in three boats sped toward depots and blew themselves up, killing themselves, two American sailors and coast guardsman but not causing extensive damage to terminals; but it served notice that depots are under threat by someone with deep knowledge of Iraqi oil industry; Prime Min Iyad Allawi says sabotage attacks on pipelines crisscrossing desert mainland has already cost nation $200 million in lost revenue; broken pipelines can be fixed in few days, but any severe damage to giant, isolated oil terminals could be devastating to country counting on its oil wealth as best hope for stable future; photos; map (M)
news.title: 15 Miles Offshore, Safeguarding Iraq's Oil Lifeline

news.abstract: INTRO
news.title: Transcript of Palestine Lost

news.abstract: UN reports that proportion of world's new HIV infections occurring in Asia has risen sharply in past two years; nearly 1.2 million of estimated 4.8 new infections in 2003 occurred in Asia; photo; graph; rate of new infection worldwide was highest ever (M)
news.title: U.N. Report Shows Concern Over Rise of H.I.V. in Asia

news.abstract: Former Pres Jimmy Carter, in Jakarta, declares himself satisfied with conduct of Indonesian election (S)
news.title: Carter, in Jakarta, Praises the Election

news.abstract: Relatives of Americans killed in attacks in Israel bring suit in federal court in Brooklyn, charging Arab Bank of Jordan with aiding terrorism by paying life insurance to families of Palestinian suicide bombers; suit says bank channeled funds from Saudi government organization to Hamas and Islamic Jihad, paying $5,316 to families (S)
news.title: Suit Claims Arab Bank Aided Militants' Relatives

news.abstract: Iraqi Prime Min Iyad Allawi signs into law broad martial powers enabling him to impose curfews, ban groups considered seditious and order detentions of people deemed security risks; says forceful response to tenacious insurgency was written with input from lawyers and ministers of justice and human rights, interview; calls on Iraqis to take responsibility to enforce law and order and fight terrorists; photo; draft obtained by The New York Times quoted (M)
news.title: New Law in Iraq Gives Premier Martial Powers to Fight Uprising

news.abstract: Pentagon begins long-range planning on how to reduce number of American troops in Iraq, now that interim Iraqi government is in place; continued American presence is sore spot for new Iraqi government as it seeks to establish credibility with Iraqi people; senior military officials say that how long American forces stay in Iraq and in what numbers will be driven by security conditions and how quickly Iraqi security forces establish themselves; photo (M)
news.title: U.S. Starts Drawing Plans To Cut Its Troops in Iraq

news.abstract: Also, the abduction of a Filipino led the president of the Philippines to order citizens to stop traveling to Iraq in search of work.
news.title: Five U.S. Soldiers Are Killed in Iraq as Mortars Hit Base

news.abstract: Archbishop Pius Ncube, top Roman Catholic official in Zimbabe, accuses Africa's heads of state of complicity in prolonging repression in Zimbabwe, days after African Union shelves official report condemning country's human-rights conduct; Ncube is one of most visible critics of autocratic government of Pres Robert Mugabe; he and other Zimbabwean religious leaders forecast new violence--and new exodus of refugees from Zimbabwe--unless African leaders press Mugabe to embrace democratic reforms; Ncube is especially critical of South African Pres Thabo Mbeki, who has urged tolerance of Mugabe's government as part of campaign to promote peaceful change in Zimbabwe (M)
news.title: African Leaders Failing Zimbabwe, Prelate Says

news.abstract: Russia and Georgia quarrel over arms intercepted in South Ossetia, Georgian separatist region seeking to become part of Russia; Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov holds that weapons shipment was approved by regional peacekeeping coalition; map (S)
news.title: World Briefing | Europe: Russia, Georgia: Tension Over Ossetia
